#### **Generating a certificate**

When connecting to a server in the extended authentication mode, the user first completes the standard authentication procedure by specifying the login and password. The server checks if there is an installed certificate for this account. If a certificate is found, the extended authentication is performed (the client certificate is validated). If it is not found, a new certificate is generated.

The trade server sends to the terminal a request to generate two keys, including a [private](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%97%D0%B0%D0%BA%D1%80%D1%8B%D1%82%D1%8B%D0%B9_%D0%BA%D0%BB%D1%8E%D1%87) and a [public](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BF%D1%82%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B0_%D1%81_%D0%BE%D1%82%D0%BA%D1%80%D1%8B%D1%82%D1%8B%D0%BC_%D0%BA%D0%BB%D1%8E%D1%87%D0%BE%D0%BC) key. The private key is used for decrypting server messages. It is not transmitted anywhere and is only stored in the

terminal(in an encrypted form, bound to the specific hardware). The public key is sent to a trade server and is saved in the client record. The trade server will use the key to encrypt messages which are sent to the terminal.

Based on the account data (client name and account number), the server generates a public key [certificate](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A1%D0%B5%D1%80%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%84%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%82_%D0%BE%D1%82%D0%BA%D1%80%D1%8B%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%BA%D0%BB%D1%8E%D1%87%D0%B0) and signs it using a private key (this ensures that the certificate can't be falsified). This certificate is sent to the terminal. It will be used for authenticating the user on the server and for encrypting data sent by the terminalto the server.

Next, the terminal packages the previously generated private key and the public key certificate, received from the server, into one file (container), PFX [certificate.](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/PKCS12) The PFX is additionally protected with a password. Thus, even having obtained a PFX certificate, attackers will not be able to use it.

The password for protecting the PFX certificate is set by the user in a special dialog:

| Password for SSL certificate | For higher security the extended authorization is used on the server. To continue the standard SSL certificate will be generated.<br>Read more about standard SSL certificates<br>Please enter password to protect your new certificate. Password must be at least 8 symbols long with digits and different cases. |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Password:                    | Example: setSun57                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Confirm password:            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                              | <input type="checkbox"/> Add certificate to the Windows System Storage                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                              | <button>Continue</button>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

The following should be specified here:

- ·**Password** — password to protect the certificate.
- ·**Confirm password** — confirmation of the password to avoid typing errors.
- · **Add the certificate to the Windows storage** — if this option is enabled, the certificate will be automatically installed to the operating system storage. If you installthe certificate to the system storage, then you can choose not to keep the PFX file of the certificate on the disk, in the /terminal\_data\_folder/config/certificates folder. The terminal always checks the availability of the certificate in the system storage and in the specified folder on the disk.

A password-protected PFX certificate is saved in the /profiles/server name/certificates directory of the Administrator/Manager terminal(or in the /config/certificates/ directory of the client terminal). Names to the certificate files are assigned according to the following rule: *Login\_ID\_Name.pfx*, where:

- ·**Login** — the account number
- ·**ID** — a short name of the company the account was opened in
- ·**Name** — name of a client specified when creating the account

- ·Even having access to the \*.pfx file, the certificate can't be used without the password.
- · The certificate password must contain at least two types of characters (lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits or special characters). The same minimum length requirement is used for account and certificate passwords; the relevant option is configured in group settings, under the **Common** section.
- · Certificates are generated only during the first account connection, or if the certificate was intentionally reset on the server (via the account's **Security** section).
- ·The certificate is not checked if an investor password is used.

## **Using third-party certificates**

The trading platform allows the usage of your own client certificate for authentication if required by your company's security policy.

To use your own certificates, disable the certificate generation option in the trading platform. For this, navigate to **Security / Certificates** and select **Issuing type**: **disabled**.

![](_page_89_Picture_4.jpeg)

Next, add the certification authority which generates your own company certificates to the list of trusted authorities.

Automatic generation of certificates can only be disabled for certain groups. Navigate to the **Common** tab of the group and select **RSA Custom** in the Authentication field.

#### **Setting up a client group**

To enable extended authentication with your own certificates for a client group, open the **Common** tab in group settings. Select **Custom SSL certificate** in the Authentication field.

#### **Issuance of certificates to clients**

If you choose to use custom certificates, then your company will be responsible for the distribution of certificates among clients. You should provide certificate files to clients (for example, in person, on any digital medium, including an e-token). The provided certificate must contain a private key.

To use the certificate for authentication, the client needs to do one of the following:

- · Copy the certificate file to the /profiles/server name/certificates directory of the Administrator (Manager) terminal or to the /config/certificates/ directory of the client terminal.
- · Installthe certificate to the operating system storage on the computer, from which the client will work with the trading platform.
- ·Connect a portable storage (e-token) to the computer.

During authentication, the terminal checks the described terminal storages. Please note that the required certificate in the /certificates folder of the terminal is searched by the account number specified in the certificate file name. The account number must be specified at the beginning of the certificate file, for example, 10034\_JohnSmith.pfx. This requirement does not apply to certificates installed in the operating system storage or a portable storage.

#### <span id="page-91-0"></span>**Importing a certificate into a client record**

With extended authentication, the server compares the client's certificate with the certificate associated with its account on the server. When the certificates are automatically generated on the server, the issued certificates are automatically imported into the account.

If you are using your own certificates, you must import them into client records. To do this, go to the **Certificates** tab of the client account and click Import:

## <span id="page-92-0"></span>**One-time passwords for connecting to accounts**

Use of one-time passwords (OTP) provides an additional level of security when working with the platform. The user must enter a unique OTP in addition to the login and password every time to connect to an account.

OTPs are generated in the mobile [terminalfor](https://download.mql5.com/cdn/mobile/mt5/ios?hl=ru&utm_campaign=download&utm_source=metatrader5.help) iPhone and mobile [terminalfor](https://download.mql5.com/cdn/mobile/mt5/android?hl=ru&utm_campaign=download&utm_source=metatrader5.help) Android.

### **Enabling OTP on the server**

OTP settings are managed at the account group level. For example, you can allow the OTP usage for demo groups and enforce them for real clients.

#### **Enabling**

OTPs can be enabled for all connection types or only for web [terminal](#page-12-0) connections. Select the desired option in the **One-time password** parameter.

#### **Forced use**

In some countries, regulatory authorities require the use of additional account security measures, such as the OTPs. When the **Force one-time password usage** option is enabled, alltraders from this group will need to use OTPs for connection. Otherwise, users can bind their accounts to a password generator or use the default

authentication method. Before you enable this option, please inform your clients about the new OTP option. Be extremely careful enabling this option for the only one manager group on the trading server.

#### **Using OTPs in web terminals**

The MetaTrader 5 platform supports the extended [authentication](#page-84-0) using certificates. It protects users but works only on desktop and mobile terminals. For web terminal users, only OTPs can be used as additional means of protection.

If you enable OTPs for everyone, those who use certificates will experience unnecessary difficulties connecting to the platform. They will have to pass a triple authentication: enter their standard login/password, provide a certificate, and specify a one-time password.

In order to protect web terminal users without causing extra difficulties for other users who already apply certificates, enable the **TOTP for Web only** mode. Now, if you enable the **Force one-time password usage**, one-time passwords will become mandatory for web terminals (other connections are not affected).

#### **Disabling OTP for individual accounts**

## <span id="page-102-0"></span>**Common errors**

- · Do not add your own IP address to the deny list in the [firewall](#page-67-0) settings; otherwise, you will lose access to the system.
- · When configuring IP address restrictions for your own [manager](#page-82-0) account, add your current address to the list; otherwise, you will lose access to the system.
- · Do not enable extended SSL authentication along with one-time passwords for accounts. This will complicate access to accounts.
- ·Do not disable the built-in [anti-flood](#page-65-0) control system. It protects the system against malicious attacks.

## <span id="page-103-0"></span>**Configuring platform backups**

Data safety and uninterrupted operation of the trading platform are key points for any brokerage company. Even a short stop of a trade server leads to loss of money and reputation. Today, the ability to ensure uninterrupted business processes is one of the main requirements set by financialregulators. MetaTrader 5 features allthe necessary components to provide system continuity in any critical situation.

The MetaTrader 5 platform provides a separate component responsible for data security, the [backup](#page-9-0) server. It runs in parallel as an exact copy of the primary trade or history server. The backup server state is constantly synchronized with the primary server, enabling the system to switch to the backup server at any time. Furthermore, the backup process is resource efficient:

- · Critical and frequently changing data is synchronized in realtime. These include client and trade databases, platform settings, configurations and databases of gateway trade executions.
- · The rest of data is backed up every hour, including mail and news databases, files, executable files of gateways and data feeds and plugins.

Multiple backup servers can be installed for each trade and history server, to minimize the risk of system failure.

Always install backup servers which are the mandatory components of the platform. Trade and history servers do not create backups of databases.

During complete platform [installation](#page-6-0), a backup server is only created for the main server of the cluster. It is recommended to manually add backup servers for history and additionaltrade servers of the cluster.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/components/backup_server) / Platform / Platform components / Backup server

Before deploying a server, be sure to configure server network parameters: the password that will be used by other cluster components for connection to the backup server, as well as the IP addresses through which the new server will send and receive data. Allthese parameters will be registered in the server installation package. Thus, all other cluster components will be able to connect to the backup server immediately after installation, while you will be able to manage the server via the Administrator terminal.

The backup server state is synchronized with the primary server and thus an exact copy of the primary server is creates, which enables switching to the backup server whenever it may be needed. In addition, the server creates database copies as files in the specified directory. Thus, even if the backup server databases are damaged due to which switching to this server becomes impossible, you can use database backups from a disk and restore the relevant server state.

When configuring backup parameters, you should find balance between the backup frequency and the available drive space on the computer where the backup server is installed. The following backup parameters are available in this section:

- ·**Master server** is the name of the server to be backed up and the server login (identifier).
- · **Use this backup server for automated failover**. The trading platform provides the [automated](#page-115-0) failover [system](#page-115-0) which is enabled in case the primary server fails. By default, the platform can switch to any of existing backup servers. If a certain backup server should not be used by the automated failover system, disable this option in backup settings. This may be needed if the backup server is only used for [exporting](#page-124-0) data to an SQL [database.](#page-124-0) You can additionally disable the **Enable backups** option for such servers, to save resources required for the creation of backup copies on a disk.

The option only disables automatic switching. If necessary, you can manually switch to this backup server.

· **Synchronize journals with master server**. The backup server is a copy of the primary server: it stores the same data as the primary server, including log files. If you are only using the backup server for data export to SQL, you can disable log synchronization with the primary server to save disk space.

- <span id="page-107-0"></span>· **Enable backups**. In addition to real-time state synchronization with the primary server, the backup server creates [database](#page-109-0) file copies on the hard disk on a daily basis. Such copies enable the [restoration](#page-120-0) of the primary server status as on a specific day. Disable this option to avoid the creation of file copies. It does not affect real-time data synchronization with the primary server. The backup server anyway serves as a full copy of the primary one. The creation of file copies can be disabled if the server is only used for exporting data to SQL.
- ·**Backups path** is the path on the computer at which the file copies will be saved.
- ·**Backup time** is the file copy creation time.
- <span id="page-107-1"></span>· **Additional backups**. Specify here the frequency of creation of additionalfile copies. By default, file copies are created every 24 hours, but you can set a more frequent custom period, once an hour or 4 hours. However, please note that more frequent backups require more server resources and more disk space. This option is only available for trade server backups. Backup copies of history servers are always created once every 24 hours.
- · **Keep backups** is file copies storage period. All backup copies older than the specified period are automatically deleted.
- · **Enable tick backups**. Copies of [ticks](#page-226-0) are created once a day during a full backup. The backup is performed incrementally: the first copy stores the full data snapshot, while further copies only contain changes relative to the first copy. This algorithm significantly reduces file size. The copies are stored in the \ticks directory where they are arranged in subdirectories by days, for example, ticks\2015.11.17, ticks\2015.11.18, etc. By default, the option is disabled since tick data takes much space. Adjust the **Keep backups** parameter carefully before enabling it. In case of long storage periods, backup tick copies may quickly consume all available disk space.

For manualtick data recovery, sequentially copy the folders with backup copies to the new history server, beginning with the oldest one. For example, the backup server has the following folders: ticks\2015.11.17, ticks\2015.11.18, and ticks\2015.11.19. First, copy the contents of ticks\2015.11.17 to the \ticks directory of the history server. Then, overwrite the contents with the data from the ticks\2015.11.18 folder. Then, overwrite the contents with data from the ticks\2015.11.19 folder.

The set of backup parameters for trade and history servers is different; all possible parameters were described earlier in this section.

In addition to creating periodic and full database backups, the backup servers create starting database copies. Such copies are created before the initial synchronization with the primary server in case its database is damaged. Starting backup copies have the \*start postfix. Initial synchronization is performed during the first connection to the primary server after the backup server start or restart. After the initial synchronization, the backup server willreceive data on changes made in the primary server, in realtime.

See also: Video / How to install a [backup](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/articles/1538) server

## <span id="page-108-0"></span>**Backup of custom directories and files.**

The server enables the synchronization not only of standard platform files and databases, but also of any custom directories and files. For example, many data feeds and plugins require their own .lic, .dat, and similar files for operation. These files should also be backed up.

| Label                                                  | Value                                                             |
|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Server                                                 |                                                                   |
|                                                        |                                                                   |
| Common                                                 | Network                                                           |
| Backup                                                 | SQL Export                                                        |
| SQL Options                                            |                                                                   |
| Folders                                                |                                                                   |
| Service                                                |                                                                   |
|                                                        |                                                                   |
| Please specify additional folders for synchronization. |                                                                   |
| Folder                                                 |                                                                   |
|                                                        | ab \Plugins\TradePlugin\Settings                                  |
|                                                        |                                                                   |
| Add                                                    |                                                                   |
| Edit                                                   |                                                                   |
| Delete                                                 |                                                                   |
|                                                        |                                                                   |
|                                                        |                                                                   |
|                                                        | <button>OK</button> <button>Cancel</button> <button>Help</button> |

Specify custom directories to be backed up, on the **Folders** tab.

- · **Folder**. Paths are defined relative to the primary server. Subfolders are not backed up. You should specify them explicitly to enable backup.
- · **Masks**. Specify a comma-separated list of files to be copied. File names can be described using masks. If the list is specified, only listed files matching the mask are copied. Otherwise, allfiles from the directory will be copied.
- · **Exclude**. Specify a comma-separated list of files to be ignored. File names can be described using masks. If the list is specified, files from the list and the ones matching the mask will be skipped.

Example:

```
Folder=plugins\HistoryPlugin
Masks=EURUSD*.*,*.lic,*.dat;
Exclude=*.log,*.tmp
```

Files with the .lic and .dat extensions, and files beginning with EURUSD are synchronized in the <server\_installation\_directory>\plugins\HistoryPlugin folder, while .log and .tmp files are skipped.

## <span id="page-109-0"></span>**Periodic and file copies**

A backup server is a complete copy of the primary server. Its directory contains the same folders as the primary server. The only exception concerns the *logs* folder which contains journal entries and crash logs of the backup server. In addition, the following executable files are available in the directory:

- ·**mt5srvupdater64.exe** is the executable file of the backup server update symbol.
- ·**mt5archive.exe** is the archiver which is used to compress and uncompress backup databases.
- ·**mt5backup64.exe** is the executable file of the backup server.

Thus, in case of a failure, the backup server is ready to start performing allthe functions of the primary server.

The main data of trade and history servers is backed up in realtime. These include user database, trade databases, and platform settings.

| Data                                      | Trade server                                                                                                                                                                                                               | History server                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|-------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Critical (real time<br>backup)            | User database<br>Order database<br>Deal database<br>Configuration databases                                                                                                                                                | Trade execution (executions) and<br>custom settings (settings.dat)<br>databases of running gateways                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Non-critical (backup<br>every hour)       | Files mt5sendmail64.exe and<br>mt5trade64.exe<br>Plugins (DLL, INI, DAT files, including<br>subdirectories)<br>Reports (DLL, INI files without<br>subdirectories)<br>Templates (HTML, HTM files without<br>subdirectories) | Tick history (minute bars are<br>completed directly at the backup<br>server)<br>mt5history(64).exe file<br>Gateways and datafeeds (EXE, DLL,<br>INI, DAT, JAR, CMD, BAT, PS1, VBS,<br>and PY files, including subdirectories)<br>Plugins (DLL, INI, DAT files, including<br>subdirectories) |
|                                           | User directories and files specified in the Folders section in backup server<br>settings                                                                                                                                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Non-critical (backup<br>every five hours) | Archive databases<br>Mail database<br>Daily reports database                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

Some non-criticaltrade and history server data is backed up on an hourly basis.

### **File copies**

In addition to real-time state synchronization with the primary server, the backup server creates database file copies on a disk as of certain points in time. File saving path, creation time and frequency, are specified in backup server [settings.](#page-107-0)

To save time and drive space, backups are performed incrementally:

- · The first backup copy is created for all data of the primary server. This copy is saved under the [Copy saving path]\base\ directory. The folder and file structure in this directory is fully consistent with the primary server.
- · Every next day (hour or 4 hours, depending on the [Additional](#page-107-1) parameter) , an incremental data copy is created. Such a copy contains only the changes as compared to the first (base) copy. Such copies are saved under [Copy saving path]\[YYYY.MM.DD\_HH.MM.SS]\ directories.

Thus, the server doesn't need to copy allthe data during each backup.

Consider an example of a deals database. Backup was enabled on 2019.11.06. The server created a database copy on this day. It appears on the left in the figure below. The entire history of deals is contained under the 'base' directory. It's divided by months and is presented as .zip files. During the next day, traders performed deals through the platform, while the administrator edited a trade which was executed in January 2019. On the next day, the backup server created an incremental copy in the folder named 2019.11.07\_17.10.00 (on the right). Only two .zip archives are included in the incremental copy directory. These are the archive that have changed relative to the base copy.

![](_page_110_Figure_6.jpeg)

The server can automatically delete old copies to ensure that the backups do not take up allthe free space on the drive. Backup storage depth can be set using the **Keep backups** option in the backup server settings. An old copy is applied to the base backup before being deleted. Appropriate files are merged with the files from the /**base** directory. After that, the state of the /**base** directory will be identicalto the database state as at the

time of the appropriate incremental copy. Further incremental copies are created relative to the new base copy. This approach reduces the amount of data being copied during backup procedures.

Consider this procedure using the previous example. Suppose, the **Keep backups** parameter is set to 3 days.

- · On 2019.11.06, the backup was enabled and the server created a backup copy ("base" folder). For the next three days, the server was creating incremental copies in separated folders.
- · On 2019.11.11, when it was time to create the next copy, the server copied data from the incremental archive of 2019.11.07 into the base copy.

![](_page_111_Figure_5.jpeg)

Then, the incremental archive of 2019.11.07 was deleted, while the incremental archive dated 2019.11.11 was created based on the updated base copy.

![](_page_112_Figure_1.jpeg)

In addition to backup copies, the server saves the mt5backupinfo.txt file in the [backup server installation directory]\base\ folder. The file contains information about the backup. Don't delete or modify this file. The file isn't required for [database](#page-121-0) recovery, so its copying is optional.

By using the **Enable backups** parameter, you can completely disable the creation of backups on your computer drive. This doesn't disable the synchronization of the backup server status with the primary server. The backup server stillremains its full copy. Disabling of copying to drive may be needed if the backup server is used only for data [export](#page-124-0) to SQL.

#### **Working with file copies**

To save the database status as of a certain point in time (for example, in order to move it to a long-term archive on another server), simply copy the basic and incremental copies for the desired date. Together, they represent the complete database status of the primary up server as of the certain point in time.

To query data from a file copy, open the desired MetaTrader 5 Administrator section, such as Orders, Deals, Positions, Trading accounts, and select the copy for the required date in the query box. The terminal will collect and present data from the basic and selected incremental copies. Such queries actually restore the state of the database as at the selected point in time.

### **Transferring current day logs**

The backup server is a copy of the primary server it backs up: it stores the same data and has the same file and directory structure. It also stores its logs in directories and files with the same names (Logs\\*.log)

A special mechanism prevents mixing of the servers' current day logs when switching to the backup server.

When switching the servers, the current day log file of the previous primary server is renamed by adding the .failover extension to its name. The backup server, to which the platform switches, starts its current day log from scratch. The \*.failover file is generated only on the server which previously run as primary. The server, to which the switching is performed, will create its log file from scratch.

If a reverse switching is performed the same day, the .failover file will be renamed back to .log and the backup server will continue logging in it.

Consider an example of switching the main trade server to the backup one and vice versa.

#### **Abnormal situations during backup**

The backup creation process can be tracked by the server journal. This section provides sample log entries describing unexpected situations during the backup process.

2012.06.13 17:19:57 TradeOrders: invalid index header timestamp

Such a log entry means that the order database index (order.idx) doesn't match the data in the order database (order.dat). Such a record can appear as a result of an incorrect shutdown of the backup server (for example, a power outage or a manual shutdown of the server service).

This situation is not dangerous. The backup server willrebuild the index and resume operation. This doesn't affect data in the database. However, you should find reasons for the unexpected server shutdown.

2012.06.13 17:19:57 TradeDeals: deals\_2012.06.dat: base has invalid hash

This log means that after synchronization, the deals database on the backup server differs from the relevant database on the trade server. In this case, the backup server will delete the specified database and resynchronize it.

For the deals database (deals\_\*), such log records can be normal after the weekend (when the database is optimized and compacted on the main server). The reason is that after database optimization on the trade server, the backup server sometimes can't synchronize the monthly deals database in the resource saving mode (delete the records which were deleted during optimization on the trade server). In this case, the backup server performs a full database synchronization.

For other databases, this situation is always unacceptable.

## <span id="page-115-0"></span>**Configuring the automatic failover process**

MetaTrader 5 features built-in automatic monitoring of the availability of trade and history servers. The monitoring is performed by the backup server itself as well as by access servers. Each server monitors the availability of the main server and polls other monitoring servers to check whether the main server is available to them.

If the main server is unavailable for a certain time, the platform will automatically switch to the backup server. The downtime is minimal, and switching usually takes less than a minute.

The system includes many checks and it is built in such a way as to prevent false switching.

## **Main server configuration**

There are two scenarios for determining the unavailability of the main server:

- · The server can't be accessed by **all** access servers: if you have five monitoring servers, the main server is unavailable to all of them.
- · The server is not available for the **most** of access servers: if you have five monitoring servers, the main server is unavailable to at least three of them, or to four of six monitoring servers. If you are using two monitoring servers (the minimum allowed number), the main server should be unavailable for both of them.

The scenario is defined in the main server parameters:

| MetaQuotes - MetaTrader 5 Administrator                                                                                                              |  |   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--|---|
| File<br>Edit<br>View<br><b>Services</b><br>Help                                                                                                      |  |   |
| 86; 86; Disconnect C0; Refresh ; Restart Server ; Export ; Import ; Apply ; + ; ×                                                           |  |   |
| ;; Sort ;<br>Traffic in: 448 Kbit/s<br>Traffic out: 259 Kbit/s<br>CPU total: 5%, 16 cores<br>CPU process: 0%<br>CPU DPC: 0%<br>CPU interrupts: 0% |  |   |
| Servers<br>MetaTrader Server<br>Network Cluster<br>Trade Main                                                                                        |  |   |
| Server                                                                                                                                               |  | × |
| Failover<br>Common Network Demo End of Day Accounts Orders Deals<br>Service                                                                          |  |   |
| Failover is automatic switching to backup server in case of the main server failure. Please specify<br>the settings for automatic switching.         |  |   |
| Switch mode:<br><b>Off</b>                                                                                                                           |  |   |
| Switch timeout:<br>Server is not accessible to most access servers<br>Server is not accessible to all access servers                                 |  |   |
| For Help, press                                                                                                                                      |  |   |

If several backup servers are used for one main server, then each of the backup servers will start switching to the master server mode in case of the main server failure. The last switched server will be used as the primary server, while allthe rest of them will switch back to the backup server mode.

In the **Switch timeout** parameter, specify the time (in seconds) during which the server should be unavailable for monitoring servers, after which the system should start switching to the backup server. Also, after the specified time period, other platform components start their attempts to connect to the access points of the current backup server (trying to connect to it as to the main one).

When the system measures the time during which the primary server is unavailable, it also takes into account reasons for the unavailability. In case of a manualrestart of the server, the unavailability time is increased to include the time required for restart.

- ·Unexpected failure. Switching is performed after the specified timeout.
- · The administrator restarts the server, the system service or the operating system. Switch time is increased to include the time spent for restart. The minimum time is 30 seconds and the maximum time is 300 seconds.
- · Server restart during platform update. Switch time is increased to include time spent for restart. The minimum time is 180 seconds; the maximum is 300 seconds.

## **Configuring monitoring servers**

For an access server to start monitoring the main server, enable "Use this server for monitoring the cluster and failover" option in server settings:

| Server                                                                                                                                       |       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| Common Network Access Permissions Servers SSL Service                                                                                        |       |

| Priority:                                                                                                                                    | 19    |
| □ Enable antiflood control                                                                                                                   |       |
| Connections:                                                                                                                                 | 100   |
| Errors:                                                                                                                                      | 10    |
| Maximum news:                                                                                                                                | 16384 |
| Use this server for monitoring the cluster and failover                                                                                      |       |
|                                                                                                                                              |       |
|                                                                                                                                              |       |
| Cancel                                                                                                                                       | Help  |
| <button>OK</button>                                                                                                                          |       |

The system requires at least two monitoring servers. It is recommended to install such servers on different computers (different data centers), separately from the main and history servers. This will provide the most relevant server monitoring data.

#### **Connection to monitoring servers**

The backup server uses the following algorithm for connecting to monitoring servers:

- · As soon as the main server becomes unavailable for the backup server, the backup server checks all monitoring servers one by one and tries to connect to them.
- · First, the backup server tries to connect to the monitoring server via the local address, if possible. Connection to a local address is performed if listen addresses of the backup and access servers are located in 10.\* or 192.168\* subnet. The first three octets must be identical. In this case, both servers are considered to be located on the same subnet, and the backup server tries to connect directly to the listen address of the access server. Example: the listen address of the backup server is 192.168.0.100:1951; the listen address of the access server is 192.168.0.105:1950.
- · If connection via the local address fails, the backup server will use public points of the access server specified in its settings under the **Network** section.

For a fast switching, all access servers should be available and there should not be any disconnected servers among the monitoring servers. The backup server spends 5 seconds trying to connect to a nonexistent address.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/administration/admin_network/network_add_edit#network) / Platform / Platform setup / Network cluster / Configuring servers / Network

#### **Using several backup servers**

If several backup servers are used for one primary server, then each of the backup servers will start switching to the primary server mode in case of the primary server failure. The last switched server will be used as the primary server, while allthe rest of them will switch back to the backup server mode.

#### **Tracking monitoring results**

You can request backup server logs using the **Failover** keyword to controlthe process of monitoring. Log examples:

```
2013.09.09 09:07:33 Failover master server '1' - 'Trade Main' is available
2013.09.09 09:07:33 Failover master server '1' - 'Trade Main' is available
for witness server '2' - 'Access Point 1'
2013.09.09 09:07:34 Failover master server '1' - 'Trade Main' is available
for witness server '6' - 'Access Point 2'
2013.09.09 09:07:54 Failover witness access server '7' is not available
2013.09.09 09:07:54 Failover master server '1' - 'Trade Main' is available
for witness server '11' - 'Access Point 3
2013.09.09 09:07:54 Failover master server '1' - 'Trade Main' is available
for 4 witnesses and unavailable for 0 witnesses [0 min]
```

These logs mean the following:

- ·Primary server with ID 1 is available.
- ·Primary server with ID 1 is available for the monitoring server 2 named Access Point 1.
- ·Primary server with ID 1 is available for the monitoring server 6 named Access Point 2.
- ·Monitoring server with ID 7 is unavailable for the backup server.
- ·Primary server with ID 1 is available for monitoring server 11 named Access Point 3.
- · Primary is available for 4 monitoring servers and is not available for 0 monitoring servers. The time, during which the server was unavailable, is shown in parentheses.

#### **Switching features**

On the backup server side, the switching process is performed as follows:

- ·The backup server stops its Windows service.
- · It also updates platform network settings. Servers exchange their roles: the primary server becomes the backup one, and the backup server starts operating as the primary server.
  - · Network settings (IP addresses, outgoing address, and public points) and the name of the former backup server are set for the primary server in the platform configuration.
  - · The IP address and the name of the former primary server are set for the backup server in the platform configuration.
  - · As for the servers, only their internalIDs change. The ID of the former primary server is set for the new backup server, and the ID of the former backup server is set for the new primary one.

![](_page_118_Picture_14.jpeg)

- ·The primary server's Windows service is installed.
- ·The platform sends a notification to the primary server and waits for a confirmation.
- ·The Windows service of the primary server is launched.
- ·The former backup server's Windows service is deleted.

If the primary server was running during the switch to the backup server, the primary server is switched to the backup mode:

- ·The primary server's Windows service is stopped.
- ·Network settings are updated similar to how it is done for the backup server.
- ·The backup server's Windows service is installed and launched.
- · The former primary server's Windows service is deleted.
  - · If the former primary server was inactive when the platform switched to the backup one (for example, the server machine was turned off) and the copy restored from backup is already working by the moment the server is restored, the former primary server switches to the backup mode automatically.
  - · Physically (on the drive), the new trade/history server operates from the former backup server directory, while the new backup server operates from the trade/history server directory.

### **How the platform works after switching to a backup server**

After the backup server switches to a trade server mode, client terminals will start scanning public access points of the access server in an effort to connect to the new trade server. The following factors affect the access point search time:

- · Actual accessibility of the public point for the client. If an address is not available for the client (for example, a localIP address is specified in the settings as a public access point), the terminal spends 10 seconds trying to connect to it. An attempt to connect to the next access point will only be performed after 10 seconds.
- · The number of the access server addresses which are unavailable for the client. For example, if public access points include two local addresses 192.168.0.100 and 192.168.0.101, and one external address access.server.com (available external address of the server), client terminals willfirst spend 20 seconds trying to connect to local addresses before they successfully connect to the external address.
- · Availability of the trade and history servers for the access server. The access server checks the access points of the trade and history servers according to their network settings. Correctness of network settings determines how quickly the access server is ready to go.

It is recommended that you make the access servers having localIP addresses in their list of public points, available only for administrators and managers working in the same local network. To do this, uncheck all options except "Allow administrator connection" and "Allow manager connection" under the **Permissions** tab of the access server.

## <span id="page-120-0"></span>**Restore from backup**

If the main trade server fails, you won't be able to switch to the backup server manually via MetaTrader 5 Administrator as you won't be able to connect to the server. Also, manage other cluster components will be impossible. Such a situation can be avoided by using the [automated](#page-115-0) failover system. However, if the failover system hasn't been enabled, you will need to restore the server manually:

1. Go to the computer where the main trade server is installed, and stop the system service if it is running. The default name of the main trade server service is mt5tmsrv. It can be stopped via the Control Panel— Administrative Tools—Services or through the command line:

```
net stop mt5tmsrv
or
D:\MetaTrader 5 Platform\Main Trade\mt5trade64.exe /stop.
```

If the computer is down (is unavailable), skip this step. However, once the computer is back up, please make sure that the old trade server service has not been restarted.

2. Go to the computer where the backup server is installed, and stop the system service. The default name of the backup server service is mt5bsrv. It can also be stopped using the Control Panel or the command line:

```
net stop mt5bsrv
or
D:\MetaTrader 5 Platform\Backup Main Trade\mt5backup64.exe /stop.
```

3. Run the backup server file from the command line with the /gui parameter. For example:

D:\MetaTrader 5 Platform\Backup Main Trade\mt5backup64.exe /gui.

Click Restore in the window that appears. After that, the recovery process will start. Other components of the cluster will automatically switch to the new primary server.

|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Enter the IP:port of the server, its ID and password. Make sure that these data were registered on the main trade server of the cluster. |                                   |
| Server IP address:                                                                                                                       | 192.168.0.67:444                  |
| Restore                                                                                                                                  | $         checkmark       $     |
| Password:                                                                                                                                |                                   |

| To connect an additional server to the cluster please specify the IP:port of the main trade server.                                      |                                   |

| © 2001-2016, MetaQuotes Software Corp.                                                                                                   |                                   |
| <button type="button">Cancel</button>                                                                                                    | <button type="button">ОК</button> |

After the recovery of the main trade server, you will be able to connect to the cluster via MetaTrader 5 Administrator. Other components can be switched to backup servers in a regular way, through the interface. For example, if the history server was installed on the same machine, you can switch to the backup server by running the appropriate command in its context menu.

You can also use the described procedure to restore other servers, including additionaltrade servers and history servers. During recovery, new configuration data is sent to the main trade server. A restored server connects to the cluster without additional settings, and you can control it via MetaTrader 5 Administrator.

It is recommended to set up a new backup server immediately after recovery.

Before you launch the backup server, please make sure the primary server is stopped. Otherwise, your clients can start working with different servers.

For example, your primary server and access server are located at the same provider. The provider has issues with the Internet connection due to which the servers become unavailable. At this moment, the platform switches to the backup server. After a while, connection to the primary server is restored causing two servers to run simultaneously. In this case, call your provider and ask them to disable the primary server immediately.

#### **Recovery process**

The recovery process is performed automatically. It consists of the following steps:

- · Configuring the main trade server. At this step, the IP address and port of the primary server are replaced with the address and port of the backup server. The relevant details are displayed at the top of the window. The server password and ID remain the same.
- ·Installing the main trade server service.
- ·Removing the backup server service.
- ·Launching the main trade server service.

If any of the steps couldn't be completed, all changes made during the recovery process are rolled back.

## <span id="page-124-0"></span>**Data export to SQL and operations with DBMS**

The MetaTrader 5 trading platform provides standard options for the real-time data export to MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, FireBird, Oracle, MariaDB and PostgreSQL databases. This option enables the quick and easy deployment of data export to an external database management system (DBMS), from which you can use platform data in any popular programming language and third-party applications. This serves as an intermediate layer between a trade server and the broker's software services, which regularly access trading data. Data export reduces the trade server load related to the retrieving of the current trading data.

The export function is enabled by specifying settings for connection to the DBMS via MetaTrader 5 Administrator. After that, the backup server will immediately perform initial data synchronization with the DBMS. Further, new data will be exported to the DBMS in realtime. The following data is exported:

- ·Information about clients (general information and trading status)
- ·Current active orders and positions
- ·The history of orders and deals
- ·Current prices
- ·Virtually all settings of the trading platform (except for the working time, synchronization and spreads)

The following popular DBMSs are supported:

- ·MySQL Server 5.7 (versions 5.1, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 8.0)
- ·MariaDB 10.2 (all versions)
- ·FireBird 3.0 (versions 2.0, 2.1, 2.5, 3.0)
- ·Microsoft SQL Express 2012 (versions 2005, 2008, 2008 R2, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2019RC)
- ·Oracle Database Express Edition 11g (versions 11g/11g Express Edition, 12c)
- ·PostgreSQL (versions 8.4 — 14.5)

### **Operation principle**

Export to database is implemented on the side of backup servers which replicate data from trade servers.

Below are the general synchronization steps on a backup server:

- ·The backup server connects to the appropriate trade server and synchronizes data.
- ·After synchronization with the trade server, the backup server synchronizes data with an external DBMS.
- · The backup server applies changes to its databases and to the external DBMS according to transactions from the trade server.

The backup server performs initial synchronization based on timestamps (Timestamp field in the tables) during each connection to DBMS:

- ·Allrecords with different timestamps in the external DBMS are replaced with backup server records.
- ·Allrecords which are absent at the backup server are removed from the external DBMS.

The timestamp is used to verify that records on the backup server match the data in the external DBMS. If a timestamp on the backup server matches a timestamp in the external DBMS, the backup server considers that all other record fields are the same and thus the record update is not required.

After databases are synchronized, the backup server applies change transactions to the external DBMS. Additionally, prices and profit values for active orders (mt5\_orders), positions (mt5\_positions) and related trading accounts (mt5\_accounts) are also periodically updated.

### **Exportable tables**

The detailed descriptions of tables which the system exports are provided in the relevant subsections.

- ·mt5\_symbols — symbol configurations.
- ·mt5\_symbols\_sessions — symboltrading and quoting sessions.
- ·mt5\_groups — group configurations.
- ·mt5\_groups\_symbols — individual symbol settings for groups.
- ·mt5\_commissions — group commission settings.
- ·mt5\_commissions\_tiers — commission level settings.
- ·mt5\_managers — manager accounts.
- ·mt5\_clients — client database.
- ·mt5\_documents — customer document database.
- ·mt5\_users — account database.
- ·mt5\_orders — database of open orders.
- ·mt5\_positions — database of positions.
- ·mt5\_orders\_history — database of closed orders.
- ·mt5\_deals — database of deals.
- ·mt5\_accounts — database of trading account states.
- ·mt5\_prices — tick data database.
- ·mt5\_daily — daily report database.

- ·mt5\_holidays — holiday configurations.
- ·mt5\_network — general server settings.
- ·mt5\_network\_access\_servers — access server settings.
- ·mt5\_network\_history\_servers — history server settings.
- ·mt5\_network\_trade\_servers — trade server settings.
- ·mt5\_network\_backup\_servers — backup server settings.
- ·mt5\_network\_backup\_folders — backup of user folders.
- ·mt5\_firewall — firewall settings.
- ·mt5\_routing — routing rules.
- ·mt5\_routing\_dealers — dealer/gateway settings in routing rules.
- ·mt5\_routing\_conds — additional conditions in routing rules.
- ·mt5\_feeders — data feed settings.
- ·mt5\_feeder\_translates — translation settings on data feeds.
- ·mt5\_feeder\_params — additional data feed settings.
- ·mt5\_reports — report settings.
- ·mt5\_report\_params — additionalreport settings.
- ·mt5\_plugins — plugin settings.
- ·mt5\_plugin\_params — additional plugin settings.
- ·mt5\_time — platform trading time settings.
- ·mt5\_time\_weekdays — platform working schedule, by days.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/components/backup_server/sql_export) / Platform / Platform Components / Backup Server / SQL Export

#### **Custom data in MetaTrader 5 tables**

In the platform, you can create your own tables in databases and add your own fields in mt5\_\* tables, which are used for data export. Also, you can create stored procedures and triggers.

· The backup server does not recreate data but only adds or updates existing records. A table entry is only deleted if the appropriate entry is deleted on the platform side. For example, if a user is added to the mt5\_users tables, the appropriate user record will exist in the database until you delete the user from MetaTrader 5.

- ·The backup server only works with its own tables and fields.
- · The backup server does not create default indexes. Each index provides an extra load on the database, which can slow down exports and information updates.
- · When you create your own fields in mt5\_\* tables, do not forget to set default values (or allow NULL). Otherwise, the backup server will not be able to add new records to the tables.

#### **Installing a DBMS**

If you do not have a DBMS, install one of the supported options. Below are setup examples for connecting different systems.

We recommended installing the DBMS and the backup server on the same computer, for faster export. However, it should also be kept in mind that the backup server consumes resources. Also, you can deploy several backups for one trade server if necessary. These backup servers should run close to the required DBMSs.

### **Configuring SQL Export**

To enable data export to the SQL database, open backup server settings.

| Server       | 192.168.0.100:500                                                 |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Type:        | FireBird 2.x - 3.x                                                |
| Login:       | root                                                              |
| Password:    |                                                                   |
| Data Folder: | c:b t5.fdb                                                       |
|              |                                                                   |
|              |                                                                   |
|              |                                                                   |
|              | <button>OK</button> <button>Cancel</button> <button>Help</button> |

Specify the following parameters:

- ·**Type** of DBMS, to which data will be exported.
- · **Server** on which the DBMS is located. Address format may vary for different DBMS types. See field examples, later in this section.

- · **Login** is the login for connecting to the database. The account with which you are connecting must have permissions to create/edit/delete tables and data.
- ·**Password** is the password for connecting to the database.
- · **Data Folder** is the database name in the DBMS, to which the data will be exported. The database must be created in advance. See field examples, later in this section.

To track the data export process, request logs from the backup server journal using the **SQL** keyword.

If you only use the backup server for data export to SQL, disable the **Use this backup server for automated failover** option. Otherwise, the server can switch to the primary server mode and data export will stop. You can also disable the **Enable backups** option to save resources required for the creation of backup copies in a disk.

Next, set data export parameters:

· **Export history of orders and deals into separate tables by years**. History orders, deals and daily reports are exported to three separate tables by default. However, over time, the platform's databases can grow significantly, causing the tables in the SQL database to grow accordingly. If this option is enabled, the data will be additionally split into separate tables by years. You will have separate tables for each year for historical orders, trades and daily reports. This willreduce the load on the server by reducing the table sizes, as well as speed up queries to the database.

When enabling this option, modify your SQL queries against the database accordingly.

- · **Export additional tables for daily reports** — daily reports store information about the end-of-day status of a trader's open positions and pending orders. You can export this data to an SQL database. Please note that the export of these tables will only begin after the relevant options are enabled. For previously exported daily data, position and order information will not be updated. If you need to export all data, save data from the custom columns (if any) of the mt5\_daily tables and remove these tables from the SQL database. In this case, the backup server willre-export all daily data, including position and order information. Full data replication may take a considerable amount of time, so we recommend performing this operation only on weekends.
- · **Do not export users and trades from demo groups**. When the option is enabled, accounts from demo groups and trade operations (orders, deals and positions) of these accounts will not be exported to the SQL database. This reduces the load on the database and increases query speed.
- · **Refresh prices and trade profits every N minutes**. To reduce resource consumption, you can limit the frequency of price and profit exports. This data includes symbol prices, current position and order prices, as well as almost all data in the table of trading account states.

## <span id="page-135-0"></span>**Common errors**

- · Do not forget to configure backup servers for alltrade and history servers. The default backup server is installed only for the main trade server.
- · When setting up a backup server, make sure to properly configure network [parameters](#page-20-0) and to open all [required](#page-22-0) ports. It is important, because an instant connection to allthe required servers of the cluster will be required in case of switching to the backup server.
- · Before launching the backup server, please make sure the primary server is stopped. Otherwise, your clients can start working with different servers.
- · It is recommended to installthe SQL database and the backup server on the same computer, for faster export. However, it should also be kept in mind that the backup server consumes resources. Also, you can deploy several backups for one trade server if necessary. These backup servers should run close to the required DBMSs.

See also: Articles / Technical support [workdays:](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/articles/985) stumbling quotes and slippery backups

## <span id="page-136-0"></span>**Ongoing platform maintenance**

Any software product requires constant maintenance. The administrator must periodically update the software, monitor the status of the cluster, and ensure its stable and secure operation.

The platform provides built-in state [monitoring](#page-140-0) system to assist the administrator. The system monitors hardware load, system services, network activity, and other parameters, providing easy-to-use measurement reports. Also, the Administrator terminal has a built-in system of usefultips which assist in administrating the platform.

Another useful administration tool is the [Automations](#page-151-0) service. Use this service to set up mobile notifications about critical situations on the server in order to respond to them in a timely manner. Furthermore, you can automate a plethora of routine manual operations with this service.

These usefultools enable the prevention of many problems when working with the platform, and if a problem does arise, you will be able to identify and eliminate it in a timely manner.

## <span id="page-137-0"></span>**Start page and platform configuration hints**

The start page displays important information about the platform operation: license data, the number of groups, accounts and trading operations. In addition, here you can change live update settings and find a lot of useful information related to platform administration.

To open the start page, select the desired platform on the left side of the terminal.

![](_page_137_Picture_4.jpeg)

### **Server data**

The following platform data is specified in the page header:

·Name of the trading platform owner company.

- · Platform name displayed in client terminals. It consists of two parts:
  - ·Owner company's short name indicated in the license.
  - · An additional part as define by you. Here you can specify additional data, such as the server type: demo or live. The short name is set in the Server Name box below. After editing the data, select Apply on the toolbar to save settings.

The additional data must not look like the domain name of the server. For example, do not specify "demo.com", "real.net", etc.

#### **License information**

The main license details are shown at the top of the page. Here, you will be warned of approaching expiration date or account limit. Separate warnings can be shown if your platform is not [activated](#page-54-0).

- ·License — the website of the company for which the trading platform license has been issued.
- · License valid till — license expiration date. If payments are made in a timely manner and your platform is properly connected to the license server (updates.metaquotes.net), the license will be updated automatically. If the license update fails for any reason, the license box will become highlighted in red one month before the license expiration date. In this case you should immediately contact the support team for renewal. Once the license expires, the platform operation will stop and you will not be able to provide further services to your clients.
- · Symbols — the total number of symbols in the platform and the limitation according to your license type (if any).
- · Groups — the total number of groups in the platform and the limitation according to your license type (if any).
- · Real accounts — the total number of real clients in the entire platform and the limitation on the number of clients according to the license (if any). Real accounts include client records which are not in groups demo\*, manager\*, preliminary\* or contest\*. Only accounts with enabled trading are considered as real.
- ·Deals — the total number of deals executed in the platform.

#### **Live update**

Once of the following [update](#page-161-0) types is selected in this block:

- · Disabled — automated updates of platform components are not performed. The update can only be performed manually by pressing **Start Live Update** in the **Service** menu.
- ·Enabled — automated update of platform components to latest release versions.
- · Enabled with beta versions — when you launch live update, both release and beta versions of platform components will be installed. Beta versions precede the main release, allowing you to test the new features released in the update, as well as to test the operation of your plugins, gateways, and other additional

components. This option should only be enabled on test servers. Please make sure not to update your real servers with live accounts to beta versions.

After editing the data, click **Apply** on the toolbar to save settings.

Make sure your platform is [activated](#page-54-0). Otherwise, some of its basic features will be limited. If a notification in the upper part of the page shows that the platform is not activated, launch activation using the Services menu.

#### **Alerts**

Important alerts concerning the platform components are shown in this block, such as:

- · No connection between the gateway or data feed and the source. In this case, you should check the relevant log.
- · No connection with a platform component. In this case, you should check if the appropriate service is running in the operating system, as well as view the latest logs in the component's log on disk.

You should not ignore alerts.

#### **Administrator best practices**

This block features usefultips concerning platform operation, which will assist in using the platform to its full capabilities: which components need further setup or verification, how additional symbols can be added and other tips. When you select a hint, an appropriate Administrator terminal section is opened. After that the advice line will be hidden from the list.

## <span id="page-140-0"></span>**Monitoring**

Every minute, the platform measures multiple performance parameters and maintains the performance database allowing the administrator to quickly assess the status of the cluster components and respond to potential issues.

The data is conveniently presented as graphs for the entire cluster and for each platform component separately.

To see the data on the entire platform, select **Network Cluster** and one of the tabs: CPU, Traffic, Network Packets, Memory, Connections or Trade.

![](_page_140_Figure_5.jpeg)

Server restarts are shown on the graphs as verticalred lines. To view exact graph values, enable the crosshair mode in the context menu.

To view more detailed information about any component, select it in the tree.

![](_page_141_Figure_1.jpeg)

- · The variables are measured once a minute. Most of them show a one-time instant state of the server (for example, CPU load at a particular moment in time). The state can be different between measurements.
- · Performance measurements of different platform components are not synchronized (they are performed in different times). Therefore, common parameters (such as CPU load) can differ in monitoring results of different components, even if they are installed on one physical server.
- · On higher chart timeframes (5 minutes, 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day), the displayed variables represent the sum, the highest value and the lowest value over the selected period. For example, the 15-minute [connections](#page-145-0) diagram displays the maximum number of connections for every 15 minutes.
- · Current metrics (in the upper left corner of the graph) always display the last minute values regardless of the selected timeframe.

## **Cluster map**

The **Network Cluster Overview** section displays an interactive map of platform servers. The map enables easy platform state monitoring in terms of server loads, network delays and other metrics.

![](_page_142_Picture_3.jpeg)

The number of connections is shown for each server. Additionally, map regions are colored depending on the number of connections from them: more intense colors are used for higher connection numbers. Thus, you can spot regions with an extremely high load which require additional access points.

Hover the mouse over a server to view monitoring details: CPU load, memory and disk usage, and the number of connections. Disconnected servers are shown in red on the map.

Use the mouse wheel or the plus sign (+) and minus sign (-) keys to change the map scale.

Server position on the map is determined by the IP addresses automatically, through the built-in GeoIP database. If the coordinates could not be accurately determined automatically, you can specify them manually under the server properties:
