#### <span id="page-143-0"></span>**Processor**

- · TotalCPU usage in percentage. This parameter affects on how fast users and their trade operations are serviced. If the processor load regularly exceeds 50% in the middle of a work day, it is time to think about upgrading the computer. If the CPU load is more than 85%, the graph turns red. This value is critical. If the processor load is 100%, it means that the processing power is not enough for processing of tasks. Occasional spike loads are no reason to worry.
- · CPU usage by the server process. If the totalCPU load is high, while server process load is not very high, the computer resources must be consumed by some third-party application.
- ·Number of CPU cores.
- · CPU DPC (Deferred [Procedure](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/DPC) Call). DPCs have lower priority compared to normal calls. In a normal call, control is immediately transferred to called procedure code. With a DPC call, control is transferred only at a time favorable for the processor. While the processor is occupied by higher-priority tasks, lower-priority DPCs are placed in a special DPC Queue. For more information, please refer to Microsoft [documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/monitoring/infrastructure-health/vmhealth-windows/winserver-processor-cpudpctime).
- · CPU [interrupts.](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9F%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%80%D1%8B%D0%B2%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%B5) This parameter provides an indirect measure of activity of connected devices: from the system clock to the mouse. A large interrupt load can mean hardware problems on the server. For more information, please refer to Microsoft [documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2003/cc786359(v=ws.10)).
  - · If the totalCPU load stays at 85% or more, and the load by DPCs/interrupts is 15% or higher, this may indicate insufficient processor performance. In this case, we recommend that you replace the processor with a more powerful one, or allocate additional processors if you are using a virtual machine.

- · If the totalCPU load is less than 85% and the load by DPCs/interrupts is less than 15%, but you still have performance issues, the problem can be caused by third-party soft- or hardware. If DPC load surges unexpectedly, such load can be caused by recently installed soft- or hardware.
- · If you are using a multiprocessor system and the load is distributed unevenly among CPUs, try installing additional network adapters, one for each processor. This will improve system performance. For more information, please refer to Microsoft [documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/monitoring/infrastructure-health/vmhealth-windows/winserver-processor-cpudpctime).
- · The number of threads used by the server process. The values should be generally constant and may only change by a few units.
- · The total number of descriptors (handles) in the system. A descriptor is a pointer, which enables a program to access a dedicated resource. The more descriptors a process uses, the more resources it consumes.
- ·The number of descriptors (handles) used by the server process.

When you switch to higher timeframes, the graph shows the highest values for the selected period.

#### **Memory**

- · The amount of free RAM, in megabytes and percent. Availability of a large amount of free memory is extremely important for a server. This enables you to serve more connected users and to handle large databases. If the available memory becomes less than 100 MB, the graph turns red.
  - ·The amount of RAM allocated by the server process.
  - · The largest available RAM block on the computer, which can be allocated for server operation. A drop in this variable indicates memory fragmentation. This may stem from an incorrect operation of third-party plugins. In this case, you should disable plugins and restart the server.

When you switch to higher timeframes, the graph shows the lowest values (for free memory and the memory block) and the highest values (for the memory allocated by the server) for the selected period.

Allocation of a large amount of RAM for a trade server is a normal behavior. The server allocates and uses memory depending on the total amount of available physical memory. The more memory is available, the larger share of this memory the server can allocate to speed up its performance.

#### **Disk**

- ·Free disk space, in megabytes and percentage.
- · Disk queue length. The values of this parameter should be close to zero. An increase in the value indicates that the disk fails to timely write data. In this case you should consider replacing the drive.
- ·Data reading speed in MBps.
- ·Data writing speed in MBps.

When you switch to higher timeframes, the graph shows the lowest values (for free space) and the highest values (for the queue length and speed) for the selected period.

We recommend that you periodically defragment your disks, as well as monitor disk errors in the server log.

- ·Disk performance values are measured once a day.
- · The measurement of data reading and writing speed is not accurate. The measures are only provided for reference.

### <span id="page-145-0"></span>**Connections**

- · Connections show statistics on the total amount of all standard operating terminal connections and temporary connections made for executing trades, downloading history or news. In the quiet market, this parameter allows determining the number of online users. It is shown for the cluster and for individual servers.
  - ·On access servers, connections show the number of client connections.
  - ·On trade servers, the figure means virtual connections (clients actually connect via access servers).
  - ·On history servers, the metric shows connections of other components of the cluster.
- ·Blocked shows the number of connections blocked by the [Antiflood](#page-65-0) control system or by the [built-in](#page-67-0) firewall.
- · Sockets show the number of active sockets. This value means the total number of TCP endpoints (with a specific IP address and port number) connected throughout the operating system. This also takes into account half-open connections when there is no connection, but the socket is still closed by the operating system.
- · Waiting sockets: the number of half-open connections when there is no connection, but the socket is still closed by the operating system (sockets that do not have the TCP\_STATE\_LISTEN, TCP\_STATE\_ESTAB or MIB\_TCP\_STATE\_CLOSED status).

When you switch to higher timeframes, the graph shows the highest values (for connections) and total values (for sockets and blocked connections) for the selected period.

### **Network and traffic**

- · Incoming and outgoing traffic in Mbps. The load of the network interface selected in server settings (the **Service** section) is measured in terms of the incoming and outgoing traffic (average value per minute). The system measures the traffic of all programs running on the server computer. Unexpected load spikes can point to DDoS attacks.
- ·Packets — the total number of network packets.
- · Resent — the number of resent packets (the absolute number and percent of the total amount). Values greater than 3% indicate poor network connection.

When you switch to higher timeframes, the graph shows the highest values (for speed) and total values (for packets) for the selected period.

The **Networks** section features graphs displaying network latency between cluster components:

- ·The main server displays latency to the history server
- ·The history server shows latency to the main server
- ·Latency to the main and history servers is shown for additional servers
- ·The backup server displays latency to the main and backup servers

#### **Trade (for trade servers)**

- ·Users — the total number of accounts on the server.
- ·Real — the number of live accounts on the server.
- · Online — the number of accounts, which are currently connected to the server (in the minute of measurement).
- · Errors — the number of errors in connecting to the server during the minute of measurement (such as invalid password and others).
- ·Deals — the total number of deals executed on the server per minute.
- ·Real deals — the number of deals performed on real accounts per minute.
- ·Requests — the total number of trade requests executed on the server per minute.
- ·Realrequests — the number of trade requests from real accounts executed on the server per minute.
- · Average and maximum request time — time in milliseconds between the addition of a trade request into a server queue and its execution. Statistics on allrequests.
- · Average and maximum realrequest time — time in milliseconds between the addition of a trade request into a server queue and its execution. Statistics on requests sent from accounts belonging to real groups.

When you switch to higher timeframes, the graph shows the highest values (for accounts) and total values (for errors, deals and requests) for the selected period.

## **History (for the history server)**

- ·Ticks — the number of ticks received per minute.
- ·Depth of Market — the number of received changes in the Market Depth.
- ·Trade statistics — the number of changes in the trade statistics received per minute.
- ·Data sources — the number of data sources running at the time measurement.

·Gateways — the number of gateways running at the time measurement.

When you switch to higher timeframes, the graph shows the highest values (for data feeds and gateways) and total values (for price data) for the selected period.

#### **Performance parameters in the server log**

In addition to graphs, performance metrics are also displayed in relevant server logs. Such logs can be requested with the Monitor keyword.

Log examples:

2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor connections: 0, cpu: 12%, process cpu: 0%, threads: 1369, process threads: 94, handles: 23398, process handles: 799, disk queue: 0 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor net in: 272 kb/s, 16366 kb, net out: 17 kb/s, 1077 kb, retransmit: 0.109% (22 of 20081 packets), sockets: 162 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor ticks: 17755, requests: 0 (real: 0), executions 0 (processed: 0), deals: 0 (real: 0, auto: 0, manual: 0, gateway: 0) 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor users: 6999, real: 8, online: 0 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor transactions symbols: 0, groups: 0, users: 0, orders: 0, history: 0, deals\positions: 0, requests: 0 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor trade request processed income: 0, checked: 0, locked: 0 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor trade request queue income: 0, checked: 0, waiting: 0, locked: 0 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor base cache miss users: 0, deals: 0 months: 0, history: 0 months: 0, daily: 0 months: 0 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor total packets: 20, external contexts: 8, internal contexts: 13, session commands: 0 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor memory available: 40697 Mb, memory commit: 3362 Mb, max region: 40697 Mb, system commit: 25895 / 69631 Mb 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor allocators: 102216 Kb (fragments: 59, used 92270 Kb, free: 9946 Kb, items: 136013) 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor clients index: 28 kb, search index: 15 Kb, cache: 0 kb, cache miss: 0) 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor documents index: 26 kb, search index: 26 Kb, cache: 0 kb, cache miss: 0) 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor comments index: 5 kb, search index: 4 Kb, cache: 0 kb, cache miss: 0) 2018.11.23 02:51:01.657 Monitor files index: 26 kb, search index: 15 Kb, cache: 0 kb, cache miss: 0)

The logs contain the following data:

- ·connections — number of the current server connections.
- ·blocked — number of connections blocked by the anti-flood control system.
- ·trades — number of trades since the last time the status data has been collected.
- ·cpu — current CPU load in %.

- · dpc cpu — CPU load when handling deferred procedure calls. Please see the the [Processor](#page-143-0) section for further details.
- · interrupt cpu — CPU load when handling interrupts from devices. Please see the the [Processor](#page-143-0) section for further details.
- ·process cpu — current CPU usage by the server process in %.
- ·threads — number of threads.
- ·process threads — number of threads used by the server process.
- ·handles — number of system descriptors.
- ·process handles — number of system descriptors used by the server process.
- ·disk queue — disk queue length.
- ·net in — the amount of incoming traffic in kilobits, on the adapter selected for measurement.
- ·net out — the amount of outgoing traffic in kilobits, on the adapter selected for measurement.
- ·retransmit — number of retransmitted packets.
- ·sockets — total number of sockets in the operating system.
- ·ticks — number of ticks received per minute.
- ·requests — total number of trade requests executed on the server per minute.
- ·executions — number of trade executions received per minute (of which processed).
- · deals — total number of deals executed on the server per minute (of which deals from real clients processed in automatic mode, processed manually and processed by the gateway).
- · request time avg — average request processing time in milliseconds: for allrequests and for requests from real accounts.
- · tick apply time avg — average time of one tick application. This includes all operations related to the recalculation of the account trading state and of floating profit for orders and positions.
- ·users — total number of accounts on the server (of which real, of which currently online).
- · transactions — number of changes made in symbol configurations, in account data, in open/closed deals, in deals/positions and trade requests.
- · trade request processed — number of processed trade requests: incoming, verified and captured from the queue.
- · trade request queue — state of the trade server request queue. An increase in the queue may indicate that the server does not have enough resources to process requests on time. income — incoming requests which has not yet been processed; checked — the requests which have been checked; waiting — requests awaiting execution, locked — requests captured by dealers and gateways for processing.

- · automation trigger queue — number of triggered [automation](#page-151-0) triggers. activated — number of activated tasks; action queue — the number of tasks awaiting action; executed — the number of executed requests.
- · users, deals, history, daily, report — size of databases of users, deals, orders, daily reports and server reports. This section also provides information about the number of entries in the databases and the cache size (entries from databases which the server keeps in memory).
- · base cache miss — number of misses when accessing the databases of users, deals, historical orders and daily reports. A miss occurs when the server accesses data in the cache, but that data is not in the cache (for example, it has been evicted by other data). In the event of a miss, the server has to access the disk and to load the requested data into the cache, which reduces the overall system performance. The 'months' data reflect the number of misses when accessing the corresponding monthly database (user and trade data is stored on a disk in separate files by month). Actually, this is the number of calls to monthly databases on disk.

A large number of misses may indicate insufficient RAM and suboptimal database access. A large number of misses at server startup is a normal behavior (there is no data in the cache yet).

· index cache state — the record is displayed when a database index is evicted from the cache. This happens when the server needs to load new data into the cache (the index of the database that the user has accessed), but there is not enough space for this data. In this case, currently unused data is unloaded from memory. Statistics of the unloaded index is written to the server log: name, number of hits, last access time and size.

An example of such logs is shown [below.](#page-150-0)

- · clients index — size of the client database index, its search index, size of client data in cache and number of misses (similar to 'base cache miss').
- · documents index — size of the document database index, its search index, size of document data in cache and number of misses (similar to 'base cache miss').
- · comments index — size of the comment database index, its search index, size of comment data in cache and number of misses (similar to 'base cache miss').
- · files index — size of the file database index, its search index, size of file data in cache and number of misses (similar to 'base cache miss').
- ·total packets — number of network packets in the system at the dime of data measurement.
- ·external contexts — external connections.
- ·internal contexts — internal connections.
- ·session commands — internal parameter displaying the number of unprocessed commands.
- ·async requests — number of asynchronous requests.
- · memory available — the lesser of two values:
  - ·total size of free memory blocks available for the process,

- ·size of the available (free) physical memory.
- ·memory commit — total volume of the memory blocks allocated to the process.
- · max region — size of the maximum continuous free memory block (overall memory fragmentation parameter).
- ·system commit — total volume of the memory blocks allocated for the operation of the operating system.
- ·allocators — data on the the internal state of memory (this parameter is used only by the developers).

Performance metrics are measured and written to the journal once a minute. Performance measurements of different platform components are not synchronized (they are performed in different times).

#### <span id="page-150-0"></span>**A log example with data about server operations with the trade cache**

Trading history is stored on the server disk grouped by months. When data of a certain month is accessed, the server loads the minimum month description, i.e. the index, to its memory. The collection of monthly indexes loaded into server memory is the monthly data cache. The cache information is periodically printed to the server log:

07:00:05.119 Monitor deals months: 36646 Mb / 33 records, month miss: 0, cache: 15077 Mb / 23525376 records, cache miss: 15

This record shows information on the database itself (the first part) and on the cache (the second part): size, number of months and number of missed access attempts.

Cache misses occur when the required month is not in memory, and its index has to be loaded from disk - this can possibly evict another month due to the limited memory.

When data is evicted, statistics of each month is printed to log:

```
index cache state: deals_YYYY.MM.dat: index cache state: XXX hits, last access: XXX,
size: XXX mb
```

The log displays the name, the number of hits, last access date and size.

The presence of three or more misses in a monthly cache ('months miss') or 500 or more misses in the read cache ('cache miss') may indicate:

- · The need to increase memory for the server. Index data take up a lot of space, therefore, the cache can contain few months. Before making a decision, you should additionally check how many months are loaded into memory.
- · A client (plugin\report\manager\terminal), who accesses deep trading history or requests a bulk of deals from different months. In this case, you should find the source of such requests.

## <span id="page-151-0"></span>**Automation of administrator operations**

The Automations service enables the execution of various actions in the platform based on predefined scenarios. To automate routine operations, select conditions and appropriate actions which should trigger under these conditions. Automations streamline day-to-day company processes and eventually minimize manual operations. The service does not require programming skills from the administrator as allrules can be configured in a user-friendly visual mode.

![](_page_151_Figure_3.jpeg)

The following actions can be automated:

- · Communication with clients. Automatically notify clients when their balances drop below a certain value, send promotional emails to new clients and reminders to inactive customers.
- · Platform maintenance. Restart servers and gateways if performance metrics degrade, launch history synchronization according to a pre-configured schedules.
- · Configurations management. Set dynamic time-based symbol and group parameters or rearrange routing rules after reaching threshold volumes.
- ·Deals management. Close positions and cancel orders upon the expiration of futures contracts.
- · Accounts management. Disable trading for malicious traders, conduct balance operations and add automated comments after certain actions.
- · Sending events to external systems. Back-office integration options will be added soon. For example, you will be able to send information on opened accounts to online trader rooms or to your CRM system via the REST API.

Reduce manual operations and free up resources for important business tasks. Furthermore, automations improve the quality of services by eliminating human errors. Save money on programmer services and paid plugins by replacing them with simple and easy-to-control automation tasks.

#### **Test the service and purchase a subscription**

You can create up to three Automation tasks for free. Any types of conditions and actions can be automated. Test the system and evaluate its efficiency for your business.

To remove trialrestrictions and to add more automations, purchase a [subscription](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/market/product/547) from the Support Center. The service costs 500 USD per month, but the savings and the additional earnings can certainly be much higher than the aforementioned cost.

### **Automation for platform administrators**

The automation service facilitates routine operations related to platform configurations. With this service, you can set up mobile notifications for critical situations arising on the server. Furthermore, you can integrate the platform with your back office, such as your website, system analytics and other services.

In this section, we will look at an example of automating an administration task. The full description of the service is available in the platform [documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/administration/automation).

## **High CPU notification on mobile**

This task will automatically send a notification to the platform administrator's mobile phone if the CPU load on the trade server exceeds 70%. The administrator can quickly respond to the issue and eliminate the cause to ensure interrupted customer service.

Create a new task and select the Performance Monitor trigger for it.

Triggers are events in the platform for which automation tasks are executed. When an event occurs, the system checks the conditions in the task: if these conditions are met, the specified action is executed.

Performance Monitor triggers every time when the platform [performance](#page-140-0) is measured, i.e. once a minute. The measured values are compared with the conditions specified in the automation task.

No other settings are required in this section. The expiration date is not indicated to enable constant tasks operation; additionalrepetitions are not needed because the trigger fires every minute.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/administration/automation/automation_trigger) / Platform / Platform Settings / Automations / Triggers

The performance trigger operates in combination with the Platform category conditions. Select TotalCPU usage and set the value to > 70%. If the measurement exceeds this value, the task willfire.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/administration/automation/automation_condition) / Platform / Platform Settings / Automations / Conditions

#### **Message text**

You can use macros in messages. Macros allow the substitution of appropriate data depending on the message recipient (account) and the event. Use the context menu to insert macros.

In this case, macro #MONITOR\_CPU# was used. It will substitute the measured CPU load into the text.

# <span id="page-157-0"></span>**License restrictions: Accounts, servers, expiration**

The MetaTrader 5 platform is available in three different configurations, which allows choosing the license type that best suits your business model and company development plans. The pricing policy does not require an upfront license purchase fee, as the platform is based on a flat "Pay as You Go" monthly subscription fee. Each license type includes desktop, web and mobile (iOS & Android) terminals at no additional cost. License types differ on the real accounts capacity and the number of trade servers.

| License type      | Real accounts capacity | Monthly flat fee (USD) |
|-------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| <b>ENTRY</b>      | 1 000                  | 5 000                  |
| <b>STANDARD</b>   | 25 000                 | 10 000                 |
| <b>ENTERPRISE</b> | 200 000                | 20 000                 |

## **Entry**

The entry set of system components supporting up to 1,000 real accounts. The Entry license is suitable for companies serving a small number of customers.

## **Standard**

The standard set of system components supporting up to 25 000 real accounts. This amount is enough to meet your current business needs while additionally reserving lots of room for dynamic business growth.

The Standard license is an ideal solution for the most of established medium-to-large size companies.

## **Enterprise**

An ultimate license allowing you to serve up to 200,000 real accounts. This set allows establishing three [common](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/components/trade_server) trade [servers](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/components/trade_server) in addition to the main one. The system installed under the license of this type is able to support and satisfy even the most extreme demands.

Enterprise is idealfor large established institutions such as large international brokers, banks and liquidity providers operating on multiple markets and serving very large and diverse client base.

## **Control of the current account capacity**

The number of real accounts is displayed on the platform start page:

![](_page_159_Picture_3.jpeg)

If the number of allowed accounts is running out, a relevant notification will be displayed on this page. Please do not ignore this warning, otherwise you will not be able to open new accounts for your clients soon.

Number of real accounts is the total number of accounts available in the system depending on the purchased license type. This number does not include accounts opened in manager\*, demo\*, preliminary\* and contest\* groups, as well as accounts with disabled trading options.

## **Controlling license expiration**

The license expiration date is also displayed on the start page.

A notification will appear one month before the expiration Do not ignore it. If the license expires, the platform will switch to the reduced functionality mode and you will not be able to serve customers.

Please contact technical support for license renewal. Once a new license is issued for you, you will need to run the [platform](#page-161-0) update. During update check, the updated license file will be downloaded and installed.

All servers in the cluster are restarted to apply the new license. Therefore, the license update and download should be launched only on weekends, during non-trading hours.

## <span id="page-161-0"></span>**Platform update**

One of the criticaltasks related to platform administration is keeping the system up to date. New versions provide new features, bug fixes, improved performance, and increased reliability.

Using older versions is connected with potential compatibility and security issues. If you postpone updates for too long, later you will have to jump through several updates when installing the latest version. This may cause connectivity issues with your back office and third-party integrations.

New versions expand platform capabilities and provide greater reliability. Your company gains a competitive edge and improves customer service through updates. You can view release notes on the [Support](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/news) Center [website](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/news) to see how new versions affect the platform.

### **Upgrade recommendations**

Although the platform provides full inter-version compatibility of interfaces and allAPIs, we highly recommend that you install new versions on your development and demo servers, to ensure correct platform operation. If you do not have free [development](#page-53-0) licenses, please contact [technical](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/servicedesk/new) support.

After making sure that the new version is fully compatible and stable with all integrations, proceed to updating the working platform. Install updates only on weekends when trading is not conducted.

## **Built-in update system**

The Live Update system is a reliable and efficient way to distribute the updated versions of all platform components.

- ·Terminal updates are cached on access servers to reduce the load on the history server.
- · The update files are compressed and digitally signed. These files are transmitted over an encrypted channel.
- ·Platform components additionally check updates when unpacking the files.

The update of the entire platform can be easily installed with one command.

## **Configuring the update system**

The platform update mode is controlled on the start page.

![](_page_162_Picture_1.jpeg)

There are three options for installing updates:

- · **Disabled** — the platform is not updated [automatically](#page-162-0) in this mode. The update can only be performed manually by pressing **Start Live Update** in the **Service** menu.
- ·**Enabled** — in this mode, platform components are updated automatically to latest release versions.
- · **Enabled with beta versions** — in addition to release versions of platform components, updates can provide beta versions, which are released much more often. If this option is enabled, the components will be updated regardless of the update type. However, please note that beta versions may be unstable and should be installed only in special cases.

It is highly recommended to use the beta updates only in special cases and only on demo servers.

### <span id="page-162-0"></span>**Automated update procedure**

- · On the night from Saturday to Sunday, during optimization, the history server runs the mt5srvupdater64.exe file, which connects to the update server and checks for updates for all platform components. Optimization time is specified under the **Service** section of the main trade server.
- ·If updates are available, the relevant files are downloaded.

- ·Further, the history server notifies other platform components about the availability of updates.
- ·Server components are immediately updated in the automated mode.
- ·Terminals will display a window prompting the user to update to the latest version.

### **Manual update**

To start updating the platform manually, click **Start Live Update** in the **Service** menu.

### **Monitoring the update process**

To view the update result, query the history server [log,](#page-167-0) specifying Update for the type of requested records.

## **Rollback an update**

If, for any reason, you need to roll back a platform update to one of the previous versions, please observe the following points:

- ·Before rolling back, make a full backup of the current platform state.
- · Since some updates may convert (change the format of) databases and configuration files, you can't rollback executable files of the trading platform components separately. You should perform the fullroll back.
- · Also, please note that API versions can be changed during the update. Accordingly, third-party applications written in the APIs must be recompiled with the correct version.

It is not recommended to roll back to previous versions unless absolutely necessary.

## <span id="page-165-0"></span>**Migrating the platform to new hardware**

If you need to move history or trade servers, for example to a new hardware, use the backup server capabilities. It is a reliable and quick option.

Install a [backup](#page-104-0) server on the computer, to which you plan to migrate the server. After installing and launching the backup server, it is recommended to let it operate for a few days on the new machine, to make sure it operates well.

In order to avoid loss of data, which are backed up once an hour, restart the backup server just before switching to it. It will create a fresh backup copy of your data. During the backup process, a sync icon is displayed on the server icon: . As soon as it disappears, it means data sync is complete, and you can switch to the server. Select **Switch to the backup server**, and the backup server will start operating as the primary server, while the primary server will switch to the backup mode.

![](_page_165_Figure_5.jpeg)

Server migration must only be performed at non-trading hours. During a switchover, the backup server no longer copies the data that the main server continues to receive. Although switching usually takes less than a minute, a significant amount of data may be lost in case of large trading activity.

Be sure to restart the backup server process before switching to it, and wait for data sync to complete.

### **Changing the IP address**

When you change the IP address on the server where the MetaTrader 5 cluster is installed, binding to the new address is performed via the server [console](#page-171-0) mode:

·Run mt5trade64.exe /gui\_main for the main trade server and change addresses of all cluster components. Platform migration

- ·Run mt5history64.exe /guifor the history server and change the addresses of the history and main server.
- ·Run mt5access64.exe /guifor the access server and change the addresses of the access and main server.

## <span id="page-167-0"></span>**Working with platform logs**

Platform logs serve as one of the most important tools for an administrators. Logs provide details of all problems or disputable situations. By regularly analyzing error logs and warnings, you can prevent potential issues. Logs enable controls over information accessed by employees to prevent leaks, and more.

All platform servers, gateways and data feeds have their own separate logs. The relevant components log all performed actions, errors, and other service information.

The information is written to \*.log files, separately for each day. Server logs are saved at [executable file directory]\logs; for gateways: at [history server directory]\[Gateway | Datafeed]\[configuration name]\logs.

Use MetaTrader 5 Administrator for convenient access to the logs. Select the desired component in the tree and navigate to the appropriate tab:

Next, specify the keyword for the query, record type, event type and dates.

A journal can contain a huge number of log entries. To avoid system slowdown, the Administrator terminal limits the amount of displayed information to about 30,000 lines. If you reach the limit, a notification will appear in the query window. In this case, refine your search: specify a keyword or indicate a smaller date range.

- · An integrity control system is applied for all log files. If the file was edited on the server, the first edited entry and allthe following records will be highlighted in red.
- · When contacting technical support, always attach the relevant platform logs to ensure a prompt solution to your issues.

### **Keywords**

To analyze the server log, you can use any words and phrases which can be found in the server log. Please note that requesting a full log without a query string will not output the entire server log, since the maximum amount of information output is limited (to approximately 30,000 server log lines).

You can use the following keywords to analyze specific situations:

- ·**Startup** — information about the server initialization and restart.
- ·**Exit** — information about the server stops.
- · **Synchronization** — history synchronization. Possible errors: no connection to the server, synchronization with which is required.
- · **Users** — information related to operations with the account database. Possible errors: invalid database header, error writing to/reading from disk, not enough memory.
- · **History** — information related to working with history data of a symbol. Possible errors: invalid database header, write/read error, invalid quotes in the database.
- · **datafeed** or [data feed name] — activation and operation of data feeds. Possible errors: feeder creation error, invalid timeout, error reading data from the feeder.
- ·**Filter** — filtering quotes (quotes which were not forwarded to the server).
- · **Mail** — work with the mail database. Possible errors: invalid database header, write/read error, not enough memory.
- · **Monitor** — performance measurement and operations with the monitoring database. Possible errors: invalid database header, inability to obtain information about the computer performance.
- ·**News** — news database. Possible errors: incorrect header or database version.
- · **Access, Common, Feeders, Groups, Managers, SymbolGroups, HistorySync, Holidays** — files of relevant server configurations. Possible errors: read/write error.
- ·**Network** — server operation. Possible errors: the port is already in use.
- ·**LiveUpdate** — Live Update system and its databases.
- ·**block** — blocking and unblocking by the anti-flood control.

- · **'[account number]'** — to analyze actions related to a specific account, specify the account in single quotes in the query. For example: '12345'.
- · **#[ticket]** — to analyze actions related to a specific order or deal, specify the operation ticket with the # sign in the query. For example: #111222.
- · **login** — connection to the server with an account. These logs provide information on time, type of connection (client, manager, web terminal, etc.), terminal build and other details.
- ·**logout** — account disconnection from the server.

You can specify keywords combined using logical operators as a query string. The search string supports the following logical operators:

- · **| (or)** — logical operator OR, allows the selection of log lines containing either the first or the second keyword.
- · **& (and)** — logical operator AND, allows the selection of only those log lines which contain the first and the second word; a space between keywords is considered as the AND operator.
- · **^ (-, not)** — logical operator of exclusion NOT, allows the selection of log lines that do not contain the excluded keyword.

Making an exact search query using logical operators increases the efficiency of selection of the desired log entries. For example, the search string '5'&login allows the selection of logs related to the logging in of the manager with login 5.

Search is case sensitive. For example, search for "Session" and "session" will give different results.

### **Log types**

To facilitate search, you can filter logs by type:

- ·**Full** — alltypes of journal entries.
- ·**Without logins** — all logs except the information about the connections of users to a server.
- ·**Errors only** — only error logs.

#### **Event types**

To facilitate search, you can filter logs by event type:

- ·**All** — all events except for Live Update.
- ·**Configuration** — changes in server settings.
- ·**System** — system events.
- ·**Network** — events related to network activities.

- ·**History** — events related to history data.
- ·**Accounts** — events related to accounts on the server.
- ·**Trades** — events related to trading operations on the server.
- ·**API** — events related to working via API.
- ·**LiveUpdate** — events related to the update of the platform components.
- ·**Report Mailer** — events related to the distribution of daily reports.
- ·**Failover** — events related to automatic switching to the backup server.

Live Update logs are not displayed when you select the All event type, as these logs are stored in a separate file (mt5srvupdater.log).

## <span id="page-171-0"></span>**Server and utility console commands**

Each of the executable files (\*.exe) of the trading platform servers has a specific set of console commands. The commands allow the execution of general actions with the corresponding services in the system, as well as the configuration of component connections when it is impossible to work through the Administrator terminal.

To run a console command, open the Run window in your operating system and type cmd. In the command line, go to the directory in which the executable file of one of the servers is located, enter its name and specify one of the console commands. For example:

C:\MetaTrader 5 Platform\Access>mt5access.exe /stop

#### **Common commands**

The following set of console commands perform common actions and are available for executable files of all servers:

- ·**/start** starts the service associated with this server executable file.
- ·**/stop** stops the service associated with this server executable file.
- ·**/restart** restarts the service associated with this server executable file.
- ·**/console** starts the service in console mode.
- · **/install [/name:service\_name /display:display\_name /description:service\_description]** installs a service, associating it with the given executable file. As additional parameters, you can specify the service name for the operating system, the extended (display) name of the service for users, and its description. If you do not specify parameters, the default service name will be set.
- · **/uninstall [/name:service\_name]** deletes the service associated with the given executable file. As an optional parameter, you can specify the name of the service to be deleted.
- · **/info** shows server information: internalID, own address, main server address and binding addresses (for access servers).

Additional parameters are specified without brackets. For example: /install/name:mt5access /display:Access Server

#### **Server configuration**

If incorrect parameters were specified during the installation of some component and connection to the platform via the Administrator terminal is impossibles, you can reconfigure the components using the console command **/config**. This command can run on any server except the main trade server. The following parameters are available for the command:

- · **/main:address:port** (for trade servers) or **/main\_trade:address:port** (for non-trade servers) — the IP address and port of the main trade server, separated by a colon.
- ·**/own:address:port** — the IP address and port of the server being configured, separated by a colon.
- · **/history:address:port** — the IP address and port number of the history server. The parameter is only used when configuring access servers. It enables immediate specification of the history server address, without waiting for it from the main server. This improves the speed and reliability server deployment.
- ·**/id:identifier** — the internal identifier of the server being configured.
- ·**/password:password** — the internal password of the server being configured.

You can specify multiple addresses separated by commas in the 'main', 'own' and 'history' parameters. For example: /main:192.168.0.1:440,[2a00:1987:1:30::2a]:440.

These parameters match the parameters specified in the **Network Cluster** section in the Administrator terminal. After you run the command, the previously specified server parameters will be overwritten.

Example:

/config /main:192.168.0.1:440 /own:192.168.0.1:443 /id:3 /password:3jdaLjsQ

#### **Configuring servers in graphical mode**

To configure a server in graphical mode, run its executable file from the command line with the **/gui** key. For example, mt5trade64.exe /gui.

The same parameters are configured here as in the console mode:

- ·**Server IP address** — the IP address and port of the server being configured, separated by a colon.
- ·**Server ID** — the internal identifier of the server being configured.

- ·**Password** — the internal password of the server being configured.
- ·**Main Trade server** — the IP address and port of the main trade server, separated by a colon.

The Restore command is available in the backup server configuration window. With this command you can [restore](#page-120-0) the primary server.

#### **Configuring the main trade server**

A separate console program, **/config\_main**, is provided for configuring the main trade server. The command features the following parameters:

- ·**/main:address:port** for the IP address and port of the main trade server, separated by a colon.
- ·**/access:address:port** for the IP address and port of the access server, separated by a colon.
- ·**/history:address:port** for the IP address and port of the history server, separated by a colon.
- ·**/backup:address:port** for the IP address and port of the backup server, separated by a colon.
- ·**/password:password** for the internal password that will be set for allthe aforementioned servers.

During configuration, internalIDs will be automatically assigned to all servers: 1 for the trade server, 2 for the access server, 3 for the history server, and 4 for the backup server.

#### **Configuring the main trading server in graphical mode**

To configure the main trade server in graphical mode, run its executable file from the command line with the **/gui\_main** key. For example, mt5trade64.exe /gui\_main.

The window contains a list of servers, the configurations of which are already present on the main trade server.

To change server parameters, double click on it. This will open a standard [server](#page-57-0) setup dialog, similar to the dialog in MetaTrader 5 Administrator.

When you set up the main trade server, the system verifies the parameters. The situations are not allowed:

- ·Adding a duplicate main or history server. Only one instance of each server can exist in a cluster.
- ·Specifying an incorrect range of logins, orders or deals.
- ·Creating more trade servers than allowed by the license. These servers will not work.
- ·Deleting the main server (explicitly deleting or changing the type).
- ·Deleting a working trade server.
- · Changing the network settings, after which the main trade server would no longer be available to the administrator. For example, removing the last access server.

In allthese cases, a relevant warning will be displayed when you try to save the changes.

#### **Platform update and activation**

The mt5srvupdater64.exe history server component has several console commands which enable platform update and activation if the servers are not available for connection through the Administrator terminal.

To execute these commands, run mt5srvupdater64.exe from the root directory of the history server, specifying the necessary keys:

- ·**/update** downloads the updated files of all platform components, if there are any, from the update server.
- · **/upgrade** installs the [updates](#page-161-0) of all platform components. Running this command is only possible after downloading the updates.
- ·**/activate** [activates](#page-54-0) the platform.

For example, after you run *mt5srvupdater64.exe /update /upgrade*, the system will download and install platform updates.

The update process is logged in the mt5srvupdater.txt file, located under /history/logs/.

## <span id="page-176-0"></span>**Working with platform help information**

The MetaTrader 5 trading platform is a large and complex system with many settings and operation specifics. However, to become a good administrator, you do not need to immediately learn all its features. You can easily solve any work problem if you know how to navigate in the help information.

A plethora of reference materials are available for MetaTrader 5, including documentation and articles. The information is easy to access, as it is available online, on the Support Center website, and is built into the traders and brokers working tools. Therefore, you can access the relevant information by pressing F1 in the terminal.

## **Contextual help**

The platform Help is quite extensive. For easier navigation, they use contextual links. All elements of the terminal interface, such as menu commands, tabs and dialogs, are linked to specific pages in the user manual. The platform Help files feature more than 2,000 contextual links.

To access a specific topic, for example, on working with positions, select the appropriate section in the MetaTrader 5 Administrator interface and press F1. The desired Help section will immediately open and thus you do not need to search for information.

![](_page_176_Picture_7.jpeg)

Similarly, you can invoke help for any dialog box, tab or menu command: open a dialog or hover over the command and press F1.

![](_page_177_Figure_2.jpeg)

Additionally, you may use search if you do not know in which section the required command/setting is located. The search function is available on the Support Center website and in built-in Help files.

### **Built-in support center**

To facilitate access to information, many sections of the Support Center website are built into the Manager and Administrator terminals. You can view the documentation as well as read news, articles and answers to frequently asked questions, without going to the support website.

From the same section, you can contact the support team by using service desk or live chat.

![](_page_178_Picture_4.jpeg)

## <span id="page-179-0"></span>**Common errors**

- · Remember about the platform license expiration date. Be sure to contact technical support in a timely manner to renew the license. If the license expires, the platform will switched to the reduced functionality mode and you will not be able to serve customers.
- · Monitor the real accounts capacity provided by the license. Upgrade the license in advance if necessary, so as not to reach the limit. Otherwise, you will not be able to provide services to new customers.
- · Keep your hardware up to date. We do not recommend using hardware older than three years for the platform.
- ·Use the latest versions of operating systems and install all available updates for them.
- ·Do not ignore error messages in server logs. Analyze them to determine the reasons.
- · Do not install platform beta versions on servers with real clients. Use only special development servers or servers with demo accounts.
- · Before installing a new release version of the platform, update your test platform and check its operation with allthird-party integrations.
- ·Perform any technical work (update, transfer) only on weekends, when no trading operations are performed.

## <span id="page-180-0"></span>**Configuring client groups and accounts**

The primary purpose of the MetaTrader 5 platform is to provide access to trading for the company's clients. Clients need accounts to perform trading operations. However, before creating accounts, you should determine the account structure in your platform.

- ·Which account types by deposit size you will offer: micro, mini, standard
- ·Which account types by deposit currency you will support: USD, EUR, other
- ·Which position accounting system will be offered for different account types: hedging, netting
- ·Which demo accounts will be available to your clients

All accounts are created in groups. Groups enable efficient management of common account settings, such as access to trading instruments, authorization parameters and others. Account types are created based on groups.

#### See also:

- ·Video / Get more clients: Open demo accounts from [terminals](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/articles/458)
- ·Video / Get more clients: Increase conversion rate and optimize client [management](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/articles/461)

### **Group naming guidelines**

Give your groups meaningful names to make them easier to work with. Any administrator should be able to easily understand which accounts are included in a group.

For convenience, the names can contain region, currency, White Label name (for partner account groups) and other data. For example, real-eur, real-usa.

If there are many groups, you can group them into subfolders, for example:

- ·demo\
- ·preliminary\
- ·real\
- ·whitelabel\

Only lowercase or uppercase letters, numbers, \_ (underscore) and - (hyphen) are allowed in group names.

#### **Access restrictions by server**

The MetaTrader 5 platform allows multiple trading servers to serve traders within a cluster. Even when there are a lot of clients, the platform will balance load for efficient operation.

Please pay attention to the following features when working with multiple servers:

- · Each server has its own account, client and trade databases. To access this data, you must use a manager/administrator account created on the same server. The platform determines on which server the manager account is created and connects exactly to this server.
- · Platform settings can be changed only when connected to the main trade server. This also applies to the creation of groups and trading instruments.
- · The settings of each group include a parameter that determines group binding to a trade server. All accounts created in the group will be managed on this server.

## <span id="page-182-0"></span>**Group types**

Several group types are used in the trading platform. Groups determine the purpose and access rights of the accounts included in them. The system determines the group type by its name.

### **Demo groups**

Demo groups contain demo accounts. They enable users to work in a training mode without real money, allowing them to test trading strategies. These accounts have the same functionality as the real ones. The difference is that demo accounts can be opened without any investment and, therefore, users can't expect to profit from them. Demo accounts can be opened directly from client terminals, while real accounts can only be opened through Manager and Administrator terminals.

A created group is considered a demo group if its name (including the path) contains the characters *demo* (case sensitive). For example, demo\forex, demo-USD and real\demoforex-USD are demo groups, while Demoforex and fx-USD are not considered as demo.

To enable your clients to open demo accounts directly from client terminals, add demo groups to the **Clients and accounts** \ **Account allocation** section in MetaTrader 5 Administrator.

#### **Manager groups**

Accounts from broker [employees](#page-75-0) are created in manager groups. Manager configurations can only be created based on these accounts. Only these accounts can connect to trade servers via Administrator and Manager terminals, and via APIs.

Manager groups are those whose names (including path) contain *manager* (case sensitive). For example, manager\_CFD or manager\_real.

### **Contest groups**

This type is provided specifically for holding contests among traders. Contest groups are those whose names (including path) contain *contest* (case sensitive). For example, contest\_forex or contest\USD.

Contest accounts can't be opened from terminals, as they can only be created by the broker.

Contest accounts are marked with a blue icon in client terminals. When a trader is connected to such an account, the "Contest account" title is displayed in the terminal window header. In some reports, competition accounts can be displayed in separate groups. Contest accounts operate similarly to demo ones.

## **Preliminary groups**

One preliminary group is created automatically on the server. When a user requests a real account via a client terminal, a preliminary account is created in this group. Managers can keep track of such accounts and communicate with clients, using the contact details provided during registration. After formalizing the relations with the client, the manager can easily move a preliminary account into one of real groups, which will allow the client to instantly start trading.

You can create additional preliminary groups so that customers can immediately request specific account types.

- ·Trading is prohibited for all symbols in the preliminary group.
- ·All accounts in such groups are created with a zero balance.
- · When opening an account in this group, the client receives an emails from the template [main server directory]\templates\greeting\preliminary\.
- · To enable your clients to request real accounts from client terminals, add preliminary groups to the **Clients and accounts** \ **Account allocation** section in MetaTrader 5 Administrator.

#### **Coverage groups**

The MetaTrader 5 trading platform allows you to cover client positions on other trade servers in an effort to protect your company from risks. When a client opens a position, the broker opens a position on another broker's server. Coverage groups are provided for such trades. These groups are included in specialreports, while their positions are displayed in a separate tab in the Manager terminal enabling the broker's risk manager to control situation.

Coverage groups are those whose names (including path) contain *coverage* (case sensitive). For example, coverage\forex.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/manager/summary_positions) / Manager / Dealing and risk management / Summary positions and coverage

#### **Real groups**

These groups contain accounts for working with real money. If a group does not fall into any of the above categories, the group is defined by the system as real.

- · If groups in the system have a hierarchy, their names should contain the relevant path. This path is an integral part of the group name and it is taken into account when determining its type. For example, all the subgroups created in the "manager" group will be considered as manager groups.
- ·Do not mix signs of different group types within one group name. For example, managers\demo.

Once you have determined account structure and types, proceed to creating groups.

In the first step, it is enough to specify the following basic parameters:

- · **Name** — the name of the group and the path to it. If a group is created/edited in the root section, indicate only its name. Only lowercase or uppercase letters, digits, \_ (underscore) and - (hyphen) are allowed in the name. The name of the group defines its [type](#page-182-0).
- ·**Currency** — deposit currency for this group.
- · **Digits** — the number of decimal places in the deposit currency. For standard deposit currencies, such as USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, RUR, the number of decimal places is predefined by the platform and can't be changed. When using other deposit currencies, the number of decimal places can be set manually. This parameter affects the display of the account trading state in terminals, including balance, equity, margin, and other amounts.
- · **Trade server** — the trade server on which accounts from this group will be serviced. If you only have one server, do not change this setting.

- · **Minimum password length** — minimum password length for the accounts created in this group and for the certificates used for extended authentication. The maximum possible password length is 16 characters.
- · **Company** — name of the company that serves the group. The field is mandatory. The list of companies available for selection is formed based on the trading platform license. This may be the company that owns either the main or additional White Label.

Settings related to extended authentication and one-time passwords are described in a separate section, [Platform](#page-64-0) security.

In the **Permissions** section, check the settings related to trade server load.

Set restrictions only if there are a large number of accounts on the server and it is impossible to upgrade the server hardware. If the server load is not excessive, keep these parameters unchanged.

- · **Maximum symbols** — the maximum number of [symbols](#page-201-0) for which the account can simultaneously receive quotes. This option allows reducing server load when you have a large number of symbols. Client terminals only receive quotes for the financial symbols enabled in the Market Watch window. The **Maximum symbols** parameter sets the number of first instruments in the Market Watch window, for which terminals willreceive quotes. For example, if you specify 10, terminals willreceive quotes for the first ten symbols in the list. Traders can change the order of symbols and thus enable or disable delivery of quotes for them.
- · **Maximum positions** — the maximum number of open positions which can simultaneously exist on a trader's account. The limitation works differently, depending on the position accounting type:

- · On netting accounts, the number of open positions is considered. When the limit is reached, the platform will not allow placing new orders if the execution of such orders may increase the number of open positions. In fact, the platform will only allow orders for the symbols for which there are already open positions. Current pending orders are ignored when checking the limit since their execution may lead to changes in existing positions but it can't increase their number.
- · On hedging accounts, pending orders are considered together with open positions, since a pending order activation always leads to the opening of a new position. When the limit is reached, the platform will not allow placing market orders to open positions, as well as pending orders.
- · **Maximum orders** — the maximum number of orders which one account from the groups can place simultaneously.
- · **Available history** — the maximum number of days for which the group can request data on performed trading operations.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/administration/admin_groups/groups_settings) / Platform / Platform settings / Groups / Group settings

In the first step, specify the following information:

- ·**Server Type**: the server from which the groups will be imported, MetaTrader 5 or MetaTrader 4.
- ·**Server**: server IP address and port, separated by a colon.

- · **Login**: the number of the manager account for authorization on the server. The account must have the **Configure groups** right.
- ·**Password**: the account password for authorization on the server.
- · **Use certificate from file**. If extended [authentication](#page-84-0) is used on the source server, you will need to use a certificate for connection. If the certificate was previously installed in the operating system storage, it will be automatically recognized. Otherwise, enable this option and specify the path to the certificate and its password manually. The certificate file received in the terminal is saved at /terminal data folder/profiles/server name/certificates/. This mode is only supported for import from MetaTrader 5 servers.

#### **Importing from MetaTrader 4**

Please note the following features when importing groups from MetaTrader 4 servers:

- · When importing groups from a MetaTrader 4 server, existing settings are converted, and default values are assigned to missing settings.
- · When importing groups from a MetaTrader 4 server, symboltrading settings for the groups are not imported.
- · Groups from the MetaTrader 4 server are imported into the currently selected groups section. When importing groups from a MetaTrader 5 server, their hierarchy is preserved.

Specify connection parameters:

- ·**Server Type**: the server from which the groups will be imported, MetaTrader 5 or MetaTrader 4.
- ·**Server**: server IP address and port, separated by a colon.
- · **Login**: the number of the manager account for authorization on the server. The account must have the "Configure groups" permission.
- ·**Password**: the account password for authorization on the server.
- · **Use certificate from file**. If extended [authentication](#page-84-0) is used on the source server, you will need to use a certificate for connection. If the certificate was previously installed in the operating system storage, it will be automatically recognized. Otherwise, enable this option and specify the path to the certificate and its password manually. The certificate file received in the terminal is saved at /terminal data folder/profiles/server name/certificates/. This mode is only supported for import from MetaTrader 5 servers.

To import accounts, you should have an administrator or manager account on the source server, with the following access permissions:

- ·Connection type: MetaTrader 5 Administrator or MetaTrader 5 Manager
- ·Accounts section: "Accountant", "Access accounts", "Access account personal details"
- ·Dealing section: Access to trading orders (if import includes trading history)

On the receiving server, you should have an administrator account (Connection type: MetaTrader 5 Administrator) with the same permissions along with the permission to access group settings.

The **Choose groups** field contains the default query: !demo\*,!manager\*,!coverage\*,!contest\*,\*. This query selects all accounts except for accounts from demo, manager, coverage and contest groups.

An account having a red background can't be imported to the server. Possible reasons are as follows:

- · The account group on the source server and on the current server have different position accounting types (hedging and netting). Try to select a group with a different accounting type in the **Move to group** field.
- · The account deposit currency does not match the deposit currency of the group to which you want to import the account.
- · An account with the same number already exists on the current server or on one of other trade servers of the platform.
- ·The account number is beyond the range of [accounts](#page-196-0) allowed for the current server.
- ·The symbol, for which the account has orders or positions, does not exist on the server.
- · The symbol, for which the account has orders or positions, has different numbers of decimal places on the source and target servers.
- · The group of the account does not match any group on the server. In this case, you must indicate to which group the accounts should be moved.

Information about the reason for the account import failure is provided in the tooltip that appears on hover.

Double click on an account to view how it would look like after import. This will open a standard account viewing window.

You can disable the import of individual accounts from the list. To do this, select the icon at the beginning of the account row, and it will change to .

Depending on import settings, the login of a migrated account can be preserved or converted with an offset. For example, login 101980 is converted to 1101980, if the **Login shift** parameter is set to 1,000,000. If login shift is used, the numbers of agent accounts in client records are shifted by the same value.

#### **Import settings**

To import trading operations of selected clients, enable the **Import balance, trades and trade history** option. All available orders, deals and positions will be imported.

You can also specify additional parameters:

- · **Move to group**. Select a group to which the accounts will be imported. The administrator who performs the import procedure only has access to the groups on the server to which the administrator account belongs. Additionally, the list of groups available to the administrator can be limited in manager account settings.
- · **Login shift**. You can specify a number by which all numbers of imported account will be shifted. The shift can be positive or negative. For example, 1000 or –100.

#### **Client connections and passwords**

Random passwords are generated for imported accounts. Hashes of account passwords that were used on the source server are saved in the client record. They are used for verification during the first account connection in MetaTrader 5.

During the first connection to an imported account, the client willtry to connect using the old password. When the user enters an incorrect password (the password is incorrect as a new random password has been generate), a welcome dialog will be displayed:

After successful authorization, the dialog will not be displayed again and the client will work as usual.

You can set a new password for the imported account via the Administrator or Manager terminal, and provide it to the client. The welcome dialog will not be displayed in this case. After password change, the hash of the password that was used on the source server is deleted from the client record.

#### **Import specifics**

Accounts are imported in batches of 100 accounts each. If any account from the batch could not be imported, you will need to re-import this batch. In case of errors, the rollback to the previous state is not performed. Accounts and trades from the batch that were successfully imported before the error are not removed. Before re-import, remove them manually in the following order:

- ·Orders
- ·Deals
- ·Positions

Import from another server

#### ·Accounts

Importing may take a long time, depending on the database size and your internet connection speed.

## <span id="page-196-0"></span>**Configuring accounts on the server**

Common settings for working with accounts are available for each trading server, including the main server. These settings define which numbers will be assigned to accounts and trading operations, as well as how demo accounts will be allocated.

### **Demo account allocation settings**

On the **Demo** tab, select whether the specified service will allow the allocation of demo accounts, and how long these accounts will be valid.

Demo accounts are extremely usefulfor traders, allowing them to test their strategies and skills before moving on to realtrading. However, demo accounts generate extra load on the server. Therefore, please make sure this feature does not affect real clients.

If provided by your [license,](#page-157-0) you can set up a separate trade server only for demo accounts. In this case, you can disable demo allocation on the main server and use it only for real accounts.

Specify the following parameters:

·**Demo accounts** — how demo accounts will work. The following three options are available:

- · **Disabled** — the allocation of new demo accounts via client terminals will be impossible on this server. However, you can still create demo accounts on the server via the Administrator and Manager terminals, as well as through the API.
- · **Prolong from the last login** — every time the user connects to a demo account, the account validity period will be extended by the value specified in the **Time of demo** field if the demo account has not expired at the time of connection. Only connections using the Master password (not the Investor one) are considered.
- ·**With fixed period** — demo accounts will be valid for a time specified in the **Time of demo** field.
- ·**Time of demo** — demo accounts opened on this server will be valid for the specified number of days.

If you disable the opening of new demo accounts (select the **Disabled** option), previously allocated demo accounts will operate in accordance with the **Prolong from the last login** option.

Expired demo accounts are deleted every Sunday, during [optimization](#page-61-0) time. When accounts are deleted, the following records are printed to the server log:

```
users]

2017.06.04 03:57:02.626 TradeCenter demo clean finished
```

Trading operations of deleted accounts are not deleted. This feature is controlled by a special option entitled in group settings entitled the Inactivity period:

This feature enables the automatic deletion of irrelevant data from databases, aimed at reducing the platform load. If a demo account from this group does not connect to the server for the specified number of days, all its open orders and positions will be deleted from databases. The default inactivity period is equalto 365 days. To disable the deletion of operations, set the value to 0.

Inactivity check is performed every Sunday, during optimization, for all accounts in the group, including newly created and existing accounts. For example, if the option was disabled for the group and then you set the value of 30, the server will check all accounts in the group. If the server finds any account which has not connected to the platform for the last 30 days, all operations of this account will be deleted from the database.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/administration/admin_accounts/account_allocation_groups) / Platform / Platform settings / Accounts / Account allocation settings

### **Ranges of accounts, orders and trades**

Use different account and ticket ranges for different servers for easier navigation. For example, the primary server may use the range 1–10000, while the secondary server may use 10001–20000. When a client with the login 15000 contacts you, you can instantly determine the relevant server. A similar logic applies to the ranges of trading operation tickets.

Consider the following when specifying ranges:

- · Ranges of the same type (accounts, orders, deals) must not overlap on different trading servers. We highly recommend that you clearly plan the distribution of accounts between servers.
- · Each type must have at least one range, otherwise the server will not be able to allocate accounts or tickets.
- · The end value of the range must be 1,000 more than the maximum account/ticket number already allocated on the server.
- ·The order range is also used to assign tickets to positions.
- · Ranges can only be changed during non-trading hours. A platform restart is required after the range change.

## <span id="page-200-0"></span>**Common errors**

- · The manager has access to accounts, clients and trading operations created on the same server where the manager account was created. If you have multiple servers, you should have separate manager accounts for each of the servers.
- · Add demo and preliminary groups to the **Clients and accounts** \ **Account allocation** section in MetaTrader 5 Administrator so that traders can request accounts directly from client terminals. This will help you attract more clients.
- ·Do not mix signs of different group types within one group name. For example, managers\demo.

## <span id="page-201-0"></span>**Configuring financial instruments**

The multi-asset MetaTrader 5 platform supports a wide variety of trading instruments, such as currency pairs, CFD, futures, stocks, bonds, options, ETFs, and much more. You can provide access to thousands and even tens of thousands of tools symbols the same time.

Financial instruments in the platform are referred to as symbols. They are configured in MetaTrader 5 Administrator, under the **Symbols** section.

The set of financial instruments that you need to set up depends on the liquidity sources you plan to work with: exchanges, ECN, trading systems, other brokers. Each institution provides access to specific trading opportunities.

The following tools for automated configuration of symbols are available in MetaTrader 5:

- · During installation, the platform creates the main forex currency pairs with the quotes source being the MetaQuotes-Demo server. Later, you just need to switch this source to your own, while the trading instruments will already exist in the platform. If necessary, you can modify their settings.
- · All gateways provided by MetaQuotes can import symbol settings from an externaltrading system. When you connect to a liquidity provider via the gateway, the system will instantly import the relevant symbol settings. To complete setup, you only need to arrange them in necessary directories and enable trading.
- ·Another function enables the import of symbol settings from other MetaTrader 4/5 servers via the network.

However, you may need to create and configure financial symbols manually. In this section, we willtake a quick look at the process. Fine tuning of trading parameters should be performed in cooperation with managers and dealers who have the required specialization.

A properly implemented structure willfacilitate symbol management in the future, and will enable the efficient differentiation of access for different client groups.

A ticker is usually used for the symbol name. For example, the ticker for the Apple stock is AAPL, the ticker for the Euro to the US Dollar rate is EURUSD (short names for the base and quoted currency).

If you plan to forward operations to different trading venues which have the same instruments, you can create suffixed symbols in the platform. The suffix may reflect the exchange or the market name: EURUSD.LMAX, EURUSD.GBOT.

### **Symbol masks**

Mask \* and negation sign ! are used in different platform settings for the flexible specification of the list of symbols. For example, when specifying symbols for receiving quotes from data feeds and gateways, when synchronizing historical data and when configuring holidays.

Examples:

- ·**,\*,** — all symbols
- ·**,EUR\*** — all symbols in which EUR is the base currency
- ·**,EUR\*,!EURUSD** — all symbols in which EUR is the base currency, except EURUSD
- · **,EURUSD,GBPUSD** — only the specified symbols; an unlimited number of symbols can be separated by commas
- ·**,\*USD** — all symbols, in which USD is the quoted currency

To exclude symbols using ! on data feeds and gateways, you should specify the full path of these symbols. For example, to specify all symbols from the Cboe FX subgroup, except for the EURUSD symbol located in the same subgroup, use the string "Cboe FX\\*,!Cboe FX\EURUSD". The string "Cboe FX\\*,!EURUSD" will be invalid. Also, the exception does not work for a single "\*" mask. It always allows all symbols:

- ·Forex\\*,!Forex\EURUSD — all symbols in the Forex subgroup, except EURUSD.
- ·\*,!Forex\EURUSD — all symbols. The EURUSD symbol will not be excluded.
