Once you have determined the structure of your trade offerings, proceed to creating symbols.

In the first step, it is enough to specify the following basic parameters:

- · **Symbol** — the name of the symbol. The name should not contain punctuation or special characters except for ".", "\_", "&" and "#". It is not recommended to use characters <, >, :, ", /, |, ?, \*. Do not create symbols with names only differing in case, such as for example Apple and APPLE. Otherwise problems may arise when working with price data.
- · **Digits** — number of decimal places in the financial instrument price. After changing this parameter, a server restart is required.
- <span id="page-204-1"></span>· **Market depth** — display of the Market Depth and the depth of orders displayed in it. The depth is specified for one direction. For example, if you specify 16, then up to 16 buy orders and the same number of sell orders will be displayed in the Depth of Market. The maximum depth is 32 orders in one direction. If you set here 'disabled', the symbol will use not an exchange order book but a scalping Depth of Market tool, which

features the best Bid/Ask and prices equally distanced from Bid/Ask (this distance is referred to as the price step) up and down, which enable the quick placing of pending orders. If the Depth of Market is enabled for a symbol, its chart is based on the Last price (the price of the last executed trade).

<span id="page-205-1"></span>· **Charts** — the mode of creation of the symbol chart: using the Bid or Last price. This parameter also sets the price using which financial instrument base are formed. Accordingly, this affects what charts will be shown to traders in client terminals. For symbol charts, appropriate symbol prices must be provided by data feeds or gateways. When the chart drawing mode is changed, the accumulated price history will not be rebuilt. Settings will only be applied to newly received price data.

In the **Currency** section, define the currency in which the instrument will be settled

- · **Base currency** — for currency pairs, it is the currency whose value is measured in another currency (quoted currency). For other instrument types, it is the currency in which the instrument value is determined (in which it is quoted).
- ·**Profit currency** — the currency in which the profit from deals for this symbol will be calculated.
- ·**Margin currency** — the currency in which the margin requirements for the symbol will be calculated.

You can add individual symbols or entire categories to the list. To make the access setup process more efficient, we recommend that you properly determine the [structure](#page-201-1) of your trade offerings in advance.

In this section, you can redefine some trade parameters specifically for this group. For example, you can set a larger spread, different swaps or margin requirements. It means that you can offer clients different trading conditions without creating separate symbols.

If you set several individual settings (for example you have settings with the mask \* for all symbols and individual settings for separate symbols), each setting will be applied sequentially, from top to bottom. The default setting in this case means that the parameter will not be changed from the previous value. Example:

- ·The default symbol settings include the minimum volume of 0.01 lots and the maximum volume of 100 lots.
- ·You add group-specific settings: the minimum volume of 0.1 lots and the maximum volume of 150 lots.
- ·This setting is followed by the next one, which accepts the default volume by sets the spread difference of 5.

The last setting will not reset the minimum and maximum volume settings to originally default 0.01 and 100 lots, respectively. Values specified in the second setting will be used: 0.1 and 150 lots.

## **Importing from MetaTrader 4**

When you import symbols from the MetaTrader 4 server, existing settings are converted, and default values are assigned to missing settings:

- · The filtering level of a MetaTrader 4 symbol is written into the soft filtering level. The hard filtering level is set five times higher, and the discard level is set 100 times higher.
- · Trading volume parameters are set to default. These include the minimum and maximum volume of one operation, volume change step and the allowable total volume for one symbol.

Symbols from a MetaTrader 4 server are imported into the currently selected folder. When you import symbols from a MetaTrader 5 server, the original arrangement of symbols in folders is preserved.

## <span id="page-211-0"></span>**Common errors**

- · Do not create all symbols in the same root folder. Arrange them in different folders by type. This enables easier and more efficient configuration of access to symbols for different client groups.
- · Do not create symbol copies to provide different trading conditions to traders. Conditions can be redefined at the group level, if necessary.
- ·Do not use characters <, >, :, ", /, |, ?, \* in group names. This can lead to errors in platform operation.

## <span id="page-212-0"></span>**General platform settings**

General settings include working hours and holidays. These settings globally determine when clients can trade and when they only can view charts and trading history. Also, these parameters define the server time zone and time synchronization parameters. Time synchronization parameters are extremely important for the finance industry, since any time discrepancy in trading operations or quotes can have devastating consequences.

In this section, we will also look at general principles of working with configurations which will help you in your day-to-day work, as well as methods for importing and exporting settings.

## **Creating a configuration based on an existing one**

You can create a configuration based on an existing one by changing the key parameter. In this case you do not need to specify general parameters for each new configuration. For example, by opening symbol EURUSD, changing its name to EURGBP and then saving it, you will create a new symbol with a new name but with the same settings.

The following are the key fields for different configurations:

- ·Firewall: From, To
- ·Holidays: Date, Time, Description
- ·Groups: Name
- ·Managers: Login
- ·Routing: Name
- ·Gateways: Name
- ·Plugins: Name
- ·Data feeds: Name
- ·Symbols: Symbol
- ·Synchronization: Server

### **Group work with configurations**

To edit the same parameter in several configurations, you do not need to open each of them separately, wasting much time on it. Select the required configurations using the mouse and the Shift and Ctrl keys, and then open them for editing.

Some of the fields may be inactive during group editing. These fields can't be changed for multiple configurations at the same time.

## <span id="page-214-0"></span>**Trading time**

Timing is critical when it comes to financialtransactions. Quote arrivaltime must not differ from the time of trading operations executed at these quotes and must match the quote time at the liquidity provider. Trading reports must always be accurate as they are strictly checked by regulatory authorities.

The time settings section in the platform solves two tasks: ensuring the time accuracy of all operations and determining the trading schedule.

#### **Time synchronization**

To ensure the time accuracy, the platform verifies the local computer time with the reference server every hour. If a time difference of more than 30 ms is detected, time correction is performed. To track this procedure, request the main trade server log for the **time synchronization** keyword.

```
2021.04.16 10:06:11.850 Time time synchronization with pool.ntp.org started
2021.04.16 10:06:10.775 Time time synchronization adjusted to: 2021.04.16
07:06:10.775 [diff: -1.209 sec(s)], ping: 68.86 ms
2021.04.16 10:06:10.775 Time time synchronization with pool.ntp.org complete
2021.04.16 11:06:10.646 Time time synchronization with pool.ntp.org started
2021.04.16 11:06:10.766 Time time synchronization skipped [local time is correct],
ping: 55.27 ms
2021.04.16 11:06:10.766 Time time synchronization with pool.ntp.org complete
```

Time synchronization with the reference server is only performed for the main server: all other components of the cluster are then synchronized with the main trade server.

NTP and TIME protocols are supported for time synchronization. The reference server is specified in the **Time synchronization with** parameter.

If the reference server is specified, then the system time synchronization service will automatically disabled during MetaTrader 5 server (service) launch. This avoids conflicts between synchronization systems. If no reference server is specified, the Windows synchronization mechanism will be used, and the corresponding service will continue running.

## **Time zone and daylight saving time (DST)**

By default, the platform uses the operating system time zone. This parameter can be changed in time settings. Align the time zone with the main country from which you serve traders, as well as with the markets to which you provide access.

In addition to the time zone, you can enable or disable daylight saving time (DST) adjustment in the platform.

When shifting time, the platform uses the dates stored in the operating system time zone. Therefore, it is strongly recommended to specify in Windows OS, where the platform is installed, the same time zone and DST settings as in the platform.

| Time settings in the platform and in OS                                                    | Operation specifics                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| DST shift is enabled in MetaTrader 5                                                       | The platform will shift time within an hour (during hourly synchronization) after the time has shifted in Windows. The platform aligns itself with time shift values stored in the OS time zone. |
| DST shift is disabled in MetaTrader 5                                                      | The platform will not shift the time                                                                                                                                                             |
| DST shift is enabled in MetaTrader 5, but there is no shift in the time zone set in the OS | The platform will not time because it is not known on which date/time to perform the shift                                                                                                       |

Please note that not all countries in the world set their clocks to DST. If Windows settings are set to the time zone of a country that does not switch to DST, your trading platform will also not switch the clock. Be sure to timely update your Windows operating system, as the DST calendar may change.

- · Changes in the **Time Zone** and **Daylight saving time** fields will come into effect only after the server restart. It is strongly recommended not to change the server time zone settings during a trading day, as this may cause problems in receiving of quotes. These settings should be changed on weekends or holidays or at night, when trading activity is minimal, and the quoting flow is slow.
- ·After changing the generaltime settings, the main trade server must be restarted.

## **Trading schedule settings**

As a rule, trading is disabled on weekends. Most banks and stock exchanges do not work, which means there is no liquidity in the markets. The platform supports a trading schedule, which can prevent traders from sending trade requests in non-trading hours.

In non-working time, the server allows clients to connect, as well as to view charts and trading history, without the possibility to trade. If the trader makes an attempt to place an order from the terminal, the "Market closed" warning will be returned.

Trading is disabled on weekends by default, but you can adjust the schedule manually if necessary. You can limit any hour, even in the middle of a weekday.

The following session types can be configured here:

- · Quoting sessions. During this time, the platform willreceive (and broadcast to traders) quotes from data sources.
- · Trading sessions. During this time, users can perform trading operations for the symbol. When trying to place an order outside the session, the trader willreceive the "Market closed" warning.

Both session types often coincide in time, so they are edited together by default. If you need to configure them separately, enable the **Enable separate trading sessions** option.

Several quoting and trading sessions can be set up within one day of the week. To add a new session, click on an empty time on the scale and drag the session to the desired value.

The sliders denoting session beginning and end times can be moved with the mouse and with the arrow keys. You can hold down the Shift key to slow down the slider moving speed. This enables a precise configuration of the trading session, down to the minute.

- ·Trading and quoting sessions do not affect the ability to trade from the Manager terminal.
- ·Session settings are ignored for spliced symbols as the original symbol sessions can be different.

From the **Sessions** tab, you can also limit the symbol lifetime.

If the symbol should only be available for a specific time, enable the **Use time limits** option and specify the time range. As soon as this period is over, trading will be disabled for this symbol. If the trader tries to open an order for this symbol, the "*Trading disabled*" error will be returned.

## <span id="page-219-0"></span>**Holidays**

In this section, you can add holidays to the server working calendar, for financial instrument groups or for individual symbols. On holidays:

- ·Clients can connect, view charts and trading history, but can't trade.
- · Data sources that receive only quotes are automatically disabled. After the holiday, the data sources are automatically enabled. The news data feeds continue to run.

![](_page_219_Picture_5.jpeg)

The following parameters are set for the holiday:

- ·**Enable** — enable/disable the holiday.
- · **Every year** — enable/disable holiday repetition. For such holidays, \*\*\*\* appears in the list instead of the year.
- ·**Date** — the date of the holiday.
- · **Work time** — server operation interval on the holiday. If the holiday should not have any working hours, leave zero values.
- ·**Description** — text description of the holiday.

Next, indicate which financial instruments will be affected by the holiday:

You can add specific symbols or entire categories to the list.

Holiday settings do not affect swap operations.

#### **How holidays are checked**

Holiday rules are checked from top downward. If any rule allows trading for a symbol in the specified interval, all further rules will be ignored for this symbol-interval binding. Example:

- ·The first rule prohibits trading for all symbols on January 1, 2021.
- ·The second rule allows trading for Forex group symbols from 10:00 to 12:00 on that day
- ·The third rule allows trading for the same symbols from 13:00 to 22:00
- ·The fourth rule prohibits trading for all symbols on January 1, 2021.

As a result, on January 1, 2021 trading will be allowed for Forex group symbols from 10:00 to 12:00 and from 13:00 to 22:00. The fourth rule is ignored for the earlier allowed intervals as the check for these intervals stopped after the rules allowing trading for them. Thus, in order to set severaltrading intervals inside one time interval, you should first set a prohibitive rule followed by permissive ones.

To view how the imported configuration would look like, select it and click "View".

If the imported configuration does not exist in the platform, it will be created. If the imported configuration matches the configuration already present in the trading platform, the settings of the existing configuration will be updated. The system compares configurations by key parameters, such as group name, manager login, routing rule name, etc.

Configurations of reports, plugins and funds are bound to specific servers in the cluster. When you export their settings, server IDs are also saved in JSON files. During import, the system checks the ID specified in the file and binds the configuration to the appropriate server. If the platform with the specified ID does not have a server with the specified identifier, the configuration will be bound to the main trade server. If necessary, you can change binding in the preview mode.

- · Be careful when importing settings. This operation can significantly affect the operation of the trading platform.
- ·Settings files use the UTF-16 Little Endian encoding. Files in other encodings cannot be imported.
- · Starting from platform build 1930, all volume settings are exported in two versions: with normal and increased accuracy. For example, the minimum volume for an instrument is exported as "VolumeMin" : "100" and "VolumeMinExt" : "1,000,000" (to obtain lots, the values are divided by 10,000 and 100,000,000, respectively). Priority is given to increased precision during import. If it is not specified (for example, settings were exported by an older version of the terminal), the value with normal precision will be used.

### **Command line import and export**

The console export and import mode automates the configuration process and allows transferring platform settings without the need to write complex C++ plugins or applications.

In order to start MetaTrader 5 Administrator in the console mode, use the /console key:

```
/console /server:<trade server
address:port> /login:<login> /password:<password> /action:<command> [command arguments]
```

Specify platform connection details in the 'server', 'login' and 'password' parameters. The command type is specified in the *action* parameter:

#### **Server restart**

Command /action:restart [/name:<server name>]. The server name can be optionally specified (History, Access...). If the name is specified, the matching sever will be searched for (case insensitive). If the name is not specified, the specified command will be performed for the currently connected server.

#### **Exporting configuration to JSON**

Command /action:export /file:<path> [/type:<type> /config:<mask>]. If optional arguments are not specified, the entire configuration of the connected server is exported.

Argument /file:<path> sets the destination file path. Argument /type:<type> is used for exporting a selected configuration branch and it may have the following values:

- ·common
- ·network
- ·firewall
- ·time
- ·holidays

Import and export of settings

- ·groups
- ·managers
- ·routing
- ·gateways
- ·plugins
- ·feeders
- ·reports
- ·symbols
- ·spreads
- ·historysync

Argument /config:<mask> sets a search criterion to search for a particular configuration structure by a string mask (this may contain \*,!). Search by mask can be used for the configurations of servers, groups, managers, trade requests, gateways, plugins, data feeds, reports, and symbols. The following rules applies to the rest of configurations: if a mask is specified, the configuration should be skipped; otherwise, the configuration should be processed.

#### **Importing a configuration**

Command /action:import /file:<path> [/type:<type> /config:<mask>]. All arguments are similar to those applied to export, except for the /type argument. The "common" branch (general platform settings) isn't imported.

## <span id="page-225-0"></span>**Common errors**

- · Do not change platform time settings while trading is in progress. This can disrupt the quoting feed and make trading impossible.
- · If the platform time has been erroneously shifted forward, you should wait untilthe weekend to return to the originaltime zone.
- · The platform receives information about the Daylight Saving Time settings from the Windows operating system. Install Windows operating system updates in a timely manner because the calendar may change.
- ·Time settings issues may be indicated by "old tick" errors in client terminal logs.

## <span id="page-226-0"></span>**Feeding quotes**

The following types of quotes are required for providing the ability to trade:

- · Real-time price stream — traders will execute deals at these prices. These quotes are delivered by gateways and data feeds, which connect to liquidity providers (exchanges, ECN, or other brokers) and broadcast the relevant data.
- · Deep price history, using which traders can test their strategies and perform technical analysis. This data can be obtained using different methods: data feeds with history import support (for example, IQFeeder), a function for synchronizing data with other MetaTrader servers and a data import function.

## **Types of prices**

Three basic prices of a financial instrument are used in the trading platform:

- · Bid is the highest price at which a trader can sell a financial instrument. It is the best price at which a financial symbol can be sold.
- · Ask is the lowest price at which a trader can buy a financial instrument. It is the best price at which a financial symbol can be bought.
- ·Last is the price of the last deal executed for this financial instrument.

A financial symbol can be traded on the exchange and over-the-counter (OTC) market. Different approaches to symbol quoting and charting are used depending on the market.

#### **Exchange markets with the Market Depth**

The only source of quotes in the exchange market is the Exchange itself. Buyers and sellers meet on the exchange, which keeps records of all executed deals. Orders of all market participants comprise a single Market Depth.

A Market Depth featuring real orders of market participants is available in the trading platform for exchange traded symbol. The Bid and Ask prices are formed in the Market Depth based on the best orders (these prices are shown in the Market Watch). Also, the exchange provides prices and volumes of last executed deals (Last and Volume). Last prices are used for creating price [charts](#page-228-0) and for displaying the Time & Sales tape:

#### **Over-the-counter (OTC) market**

Participants of the OTC market are big market players, such as banks and prime brokerages. They form networks to trade with each other. Medium market participants, such as banks, management companies and hedge funds connect to large participants. Market participants aggregate prices of their counterparties or they set their own prices based on counterparties' prices, and provide these prices to clients.

Only Bid and Ask streaming quotes are used in OTC market trading, without data on actual executed deals. [Charts](#page-228-0) are based on Bid prices.

#### **OTC market with the Market Depth**

Unlike the previous variant, the broker provides traders information on volumes in addition to Bid and Ask prices, which allows the displaying of the Market Depth. The exchange Market Depth consists of limit orders of market participants, while OTC Market Depth is formed based on the broker's quotes. The broker can provide different prices depending on the buying and selling volume.

![](_page_228_Figure_4.jpeg)

Here trading does not involve an exchange which could keep record of performed trades, so no Last prices are available in this mode. [Charts](#page-228-0) are based on Bid prices.

## <span id="page-228-0"></span>**How price charts are formed**

One-minute bars are formed based on symbol quotes (or ticks). Such a bar represents a set of price characteristics of a specific minute:

- · 4 prices: Low and High price during this minute, as well as the beginning and the end of the bar, i.e. the Open and Close prices
- ·Spread, which is the minimum difference between Bid and Ask registered during one this minute
- ·Tick volume, which shows the number of ticks received during bar formation
- · Volume, i.e. the real volume of deals performed during bar formation (may not be available for OTC markets)
- ·Date and time, i.e. the minute to which this bar corresponds

One-minute bars are based on Bid prices for OTC symbols, and are based on Last prices for exchange instruments.

In addition to one-minute bars, price charts in the trading platform can be displayed as larger time intervals. The time included in one bar or candlestick on the chart, is called a timeframe. The platform supports 21 timeframes, from 1 minute to 1 month.

The trading platform only stores 1-minute bars. All higher timeframes are created based on these bars. This approach ensures compliance of data across alltimeframes while saving traffic and drive space.

![](_page_229_Figure_9.jpeg)

# <span id="page-230-0"></span>**Real-time price data from gateways and data feeds**

Two platform components are responsible for real-time data delivery: gateways and data feeds. Functionally, they utilize similar quote transfer mechanisms. Gateways are normally used when the trading requests are forwarded to an external system. If only price delivery is needed, data feeds are utilized.

Quotes arrive on the server as a stream of ticks, trading statistics and Depth of Market changes. The server forwards this data to clients, while accumulating only the history of tick data. Trading statistics and changes in the Depth of Market are not saved.

### **Ticks**

Each tick can store the following data:

- ·**Date** — tick date and time.
- ·**Bid** — Bid price.
- ·**Ask** — Ask price.
- ·**Last** — price of the last executed trade (for exchange instruments).
- ·**Volume** — volume of the last executed trade (for exchange instruments).
- · **Direction** — direction of the deal as a result of which the tick was created: Buy or Sell. Usually information about the direction is filled by the data source, a gateway or a data feed. If the source does not provide such data, the history server will add it automatically according to the following algorithm:
  - · If the Last price is greater than or is equalto the last Ask price, the price is considered to have emerged as a result of a buy operation.
  - · If the Last price is less than or is equalto the last Bid price, the price is considered to have emerged as a result of a sell operation.
  - · In other cases, it is considered that the direction can't be determined, and both directions, Buy and Sell, are assigned to the tick.
- ·**Data source** — the name of the data feed/gateway.

### **Trade statistics**

In addition to the basic price data, the platform enables the broadcasting of useful [statistics](https://www.metatrader5.com/en/terminal/help/trading/market_watch#details) to traders, such as session open and close price, highest and lowest Bid/Ask/Last prices for the day, and much more.

Calculated statistics can be transmitted through data feeds and gateways. If ready-made statistical variables are not available, the appropriate metrics can be calculated on the history server and client terminal side. The statistical variables are calculated as follows:

- · **Open price** — the open price of the last (current) session. If the [symbol](#page-204-0) chart is based on Bid prices, the system remembers the Bid price value from the first tick of the session. If the tick has no Bid, the next tick is used, and so on. Similarly, the Last price is used for the instruments whose charts are based on last deal prices. If the value is provided by a gateway or data feed, exactly this value will be used. No extra check or calculation is performed until history server is restarted.
- · **Close price** — the close price of the last (recent) session. If the symbol chart is based on Bid prices, the system remembers the value of the Bid price from the last tick of the session. If the tick has no Bid, the previous tick is used, and so on. Similarly, the Last price is used for the instruments whose charts are based on last deal prices. If the value is provided by a gateway or data feed, exactly this value will be used. No extra check or calculation is performed until history server is restarted.
- · **Price change** — price change in percentage terms. Indicates the difference between the Last price and the close price of the last session in percentage terms: ((Last – Settlement Price)/Settlement Price)\*100. Bid price is used for non-exchange instruments: ((Bid – Session Close Bid)/Session Close Bid)\*100.
  - · If the value is provided by a gateway or data feed, exactly this value will be used. No extra check or calculation is performed untilthe client terminal is restarted.
  - · In mobile terminals, the daily price change is calculated both in percentage and in points. Thus, if the calculation is performed on the terminal side, both values are shown. If the daily price change data is provided by a gateway or a data feed, only the percentage value is shown.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/client/market_watch#details) / Client terminal/ Trading operations / Market watch / How to view quotes of financial [instruments](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/client/market_watch#details)

### **Depth of Market**

Depth of Market data is represented as a set of trade orders from trading participants:

- ·Order direction: Buy or Sell
- ·Price
- ·Volume

The Depth of Market provides the orders which are closest to the current market price of the financial instrument. The number of provided orders in one direction is referred to as the order book depth. The depth depends on the data provider. The depth in the platform can be limited by the financial instrument settings.

#### **Data stream switching system and priority of data sources**

To ensure continuous price data availability for traders, the platform supports the operation of multiple data sources. If the main source fails, the platform will automatically switch to another.

The system operation is based on data priority. First, the priority is determined by the data source type. Data from gateways always have higher priority than data feeds. Priority within the types is determined by the

position of the source configuration in the list. The higher the gateway or data feed configuration, the higher its priority.

The server receives information from all gateways at once. This solution allows the instant switch to other gateways in case of any issues. For example, several gateways provides quotes for one symbolfrom different financial companies. The priority determines which gateway should be used. If the required information is not received from the current gateway within a certain time, the server will automatically switch to the next gateway providing data for the same symbol. However, as soon as the platform receives data from a gateway with a higher priority, the server will switch back to it.

Source switching can be tracked in the **Charts and ticks** \ **Bid/Ask/Last ticks** section.

Every tick information stores the index of the data source from which it was received. Index — is the position of the data source in the list at the time of tick arrival. Numbering starts from 0. The "Data source" column of ticks displays the data source which currently corresponds to the index recorded in the tick.

Data source switching can also be tracked by the history server log. For example:

```
18:32:44 Ticks datafeed 2: EURUSD activation
```

This log means that at 18:32:44, the stream of EURUSD ticks from the data source with the index of 2 in the list of configurations was activated.

#### **Possible delay in the delivery of Market Depth prices after switching gateways**

To consume less resources, the history server does not store the best prices and Market Depth values for each symbol and each available data source. For the same purpose, the Market Depth is passed from the data feed to the server in the form of changes relative to the previous state, while the full Market Dept snapshot is sent to the server no more than once every 30 seconds.

Therefore, if the main price feed stops and the server switches to another one, the server has to wait for the first Market Depth snapshot from the data feed. During this time (up to 30 seconds), the Market Depth data is not updated.

### <span id="page-234-0"></span>**Protection against incorrect price data**

The arrival of an incorrect price from a data source can disrupt the trading process. For example, such price can lead to massive triggering of stop levels on accounts, massive stop outs, which in turn will cause positions to close. Recovery from a price spike can be a very long and time-consuming process, which can also negatively affect your reputation.

To avoid such disrupting situations, the platform provides built-in tools for automated price validation.

Severalfiltering levels can be configured for each symbol, in its settings:

There are three levels of quotes filtering:

- · **Soft filtration level**. This is the first border of the range of allowed symbol prices. If a new price (Bid or Ask) differs from the previous one by more than the specified value (in points), it is deleted from the price stream which is broadcast to clients. However, if such a price difference appears again and repeats for the number of times specified in the Filter box, the new price level will be accepted, and the filtration level will be shifted by the specified value. Such quotes will be broadcast again.
- · **Hard filtration level**. This is the second border of the price range. If a received quote exceeds the level both of the soft and of the hard filtration, it is discarded from the price stream broadcast to traders. For a new level of accepted price to be set, the quotes must be repeated the number of times specified in both levels.
- · **Discard filtration level**. If the difference between prices of the previous and new quote exceeds the specified value, such new prices are definitely discarded from the stream.

It is believed that there is a certain range of permissible price data fluctuations. This range is limited by the set level of softs filtration. If the Bid or Ask price of the newly received quote differs from the relevant prices of the previous quote by the soft filtration level value, such a price is discarded. If several next quotes (the quantity is specified in the **Filter** parameter) also exceed the soft filtering level, then a new range of acceptable prices is set. Example:

- ·The last EURUSD quote was 1.50213/1.50231 (Bid/Ask).
- ·The soft filtration level is set to 150; **Filter** is 3.
- · The following quotes are received next: 1.50373/1.50391, 1.50370/1.50388, 1.50372/1.50390, 1.50374/1.50392.
- ·The first three quotes will be discarded, as they exceed the previous price by more than 150 points.
- · The last quote will be let into the stream and a new range of acceptable prices will be set around this quote: 1.50374/1.50392 ± 150.

The hard filtration level serves as an additional protection against incorrect quotes. If the newly received quote differs from the previous one by an amount greater than the specified hard level value, this quote will be discarded. The additional hard filter protection implies a more complex mechanism for setting a new range of allowed prices. For the new levelto be confirmed, the quote must first pass the soft filtration level(the specified number of quotes exceeding the value), and then it mast pass the hard level.

The discard filtration level implies unconditionalremoval of quotes that differ from the previous ones by the specified amount. Such prices are considered to be unambiguously incorrect.

To completely disable filtering, set 0 for all levels: soft, hard and discard. However, this is not recommended.

#### **Filtration features**

- · Filters cannot be applied to instruments with the [enabled](#page-204-1) Depth of Market **and** with the one of the following properties: Exchange [calculation](#page-205-0) type (begins with "Exchange") or Last price based [charting](#page-205-1) mode. Also, filtering is not applied to splice symbols.
- ·Filtering is not applied to Depth of Market data.
- · The platform automatically filters out negative and zero Bid and Ask prices of non-exchange instruments, regardless of whether their Market Depth is enabled or not. Non-exchange are symbols whose calculation type does not start with Exchange.
- ·Analysis and filtration are performed separately for Bid and Ask.
- · Filters are not applied to the first tick after a break in the quotes stream, such as after the platform restart, after a break in quotation sessions, after non-working hours and after holidays. Filtration can't be applied because the previous price is not known. This rule does not apply to other price checks, including [allowable](#page-236-0) [spread](#page-236-0).
- ·Filters do not apply to ticks added via the Manager terminal and Manager API.

- · Filters are not used at the beginning of a trading day (the beginning of the first quoting session) and after the restart of the history server, since the previous price is not known in advance.
- · In the platform, one symbol can be used as the source of quotes for another symbol. Such a source symbol if specified in the Source box. Filtration settings of the source symbol are not applied to quotes translated to the destination symbol. For example, EURUSDm uses EURUSD quotes as the source. A quote that has been discarded from the EURUSD stream in accordance with the filtration parameters, can be included in the EURUSDm stream.

#### **Filtering identical quotes**

The trading platform filters out identical quotes from data sources. If within one minute the platform receives a quote that does not differ from the previous one, such a quote is not allowed into the stream. If more than a minute passes, the quote will be accepted. The same quote is also accepted if the minute has changed. The enables the correct display of charts in a low-liquid market.

Example:

- ·13:01:15 a quote is received
- ·13:01:32 the same quote is received, it is not accepted
- ·13:01:50 the same quote is received, it is not accepted
- · 13:02:01 the same quote is received, it is accepted (the interval between quotes is less than 60 seconds, but the minute has changed)

#### <span id="page-236-0"></span>**Spread control**

The Minimum Spread and Maximum Spread parameters in the **Quotes** tab are provided for additional protection. If the difference between the Bid and Ask prices in the incoming quote does not fall within the specified values, such a quote is removed from the stream.

The check is only performed for OTC (non-exchange) financial instruments with a floating spread. OTC/nonexchange symbols are those with the Forex, Futures, CFD, CFD Leverage or CFD Index calculation types.

#### **Gap mode level**

Gap is a considerable difference between the previous and the next quote in the price stream. Symbol settings allow you to define which price differences are to be considered as gaps.

Unlike the filters, quotes are not removed from the flow when enabling the gap mode. They are passed to clients. However, this check can be used in the routing rules in order to process trade requests in a special way under the market conditions that differ from normal ones. For example, after a gap, client requests can be rejected or requoted during a certain number of subsequent ticks.

Specify a value in points in the "Gap mode level" box. If the difference between the previous and the next quote exceeds the specified value, such a difference is considered a gap. The check is performed for Bid and Ask prices separately.

Next, specify the number of ticks after the gap, after which the gap mode is disabled. For example, suppose that we have the values of 100 points and 3 ticks. When a gap is detected, the tick counter is increased by 1. The gap mode is disabled if no new price spike of the specified number of points occurs within two next ticks:

- ·The first tick, in which the gap was registered. The tick counter is set to 1.
- ·The second tick without a gap. The tick counter increases to 2. It is the first tick confirming the new price.
- ·The third tick without a gap. The tick counter increases to 3. It is the second tick confirming the new price.
- ·The fourth tick without a gap. It is the third tick confirming the new price. The gap mode is disabled.

After starting a server, the first tick is always considered a gap, since the previous price is not known. The gap counter is immediately set to the maximum value in this case. Thus, the gap mode is disabled if no gap occurs on the second tick after server start.

Gaps detection and tick calculation data is displayed in the trade server journal:

```
2017.03.16 12:21:20.323 TickSymbol 'EURUSD' gap by ask from 1.07149 to 1.07250
[diff:101, gap level: 3]
2017.03.16 12:21:20.323 TickSymbol 'EURUSD' gap by ask from 1.07139 to 1.07240
[diff:101, gap level: 3]
```

The 'diff' value shows the actual difference between the previous and the next quote. The 'gap level' value shows the number of ticks specified in symbol settings, after which the gap mode is disabled.

If the difference between the current and the next price (here, it is Ask) does not exceed the specified value (100), a message will be printed to log stating that a normaltick has arrived and the counter has increased:

```
2017.03.16 12:21:20.428 TickSymbol 'EURUSD' normal tick 1.07247 after gap by ask
[tick counter: 2]
```

Please note that the counter is already equalto 2. The tick, on which the gap started, has already been counted. If the next tick does not differ by the specified value, the gap mode for the Ask price will be disabled:

```
2017.03.16 12:21:20.730 TickSymbol 'EURUSD' normal tick 1.07248 after gap by ask
[tick counter: 3]
2017.03.16 12:21:20.730 TickSymbol 'EURUSD' gap by ask mode disabled
```

#### **Additional settings**

The **Quotes** section provides some other parameters that affect the transmission of price data, such as:

- · **Allow real-time quotes from data feeds**. Enable/disable the real-time delivery of quotes for this symbol from data feeds. If the option is disabled, the dealer can manually add quotes for this symbol.
- · **Allow negative prices**. The trading platform supports operations with negative security prices. If such a situation occurs in the market, allthe appropriate functions will work correctly. This includes the display of quotes, calculation of profit margin, placing of orders, etc. However, such market situations are extremely

after the restart.

rare, and negative values in the price stream are usually caused by an error on the data source side. Therefore, the history server rejects negative prices by default. To allow negative prices in the platform, you should enable the appropriate option.

- · **Receive market statistics from datafeeds**. This option enables the delivery of market statistics (Ask High, Bid Low, etc.) directly from data sources, without the need to calculate it on the history server. If the option is disabled, the history server will calculate the following statistical variables: High and Low for Bid, Ask and Last prices; current session opening and previous session closing prices. Also, the percentage of price change relative to the previous session is calculated in client terminals. After disabling this option, a restart of the history server is required. Statistics recalculation willresume only
  - · Negative prices are only allowed for Futures contracts (Futures, Exchange Futures, Exchange FORTS Futures). Do not enable this option for other types of instruments.
  - · When enabling the **Receive market statistics from datafeeds** option, keep in mind that the data sources must support the transfer of market statistics.

#### **Configuring price data transmit through a gateway**

MetaQuotes provides ready-made gateways for connection to a wide variety of liquidity providers, including Currenex, Integral, LMAX, FXCM, MOEX, DGCX, Interactive Brokers, and others. One of the gateways enables connection to other MetaTrader 5 servers. It means that any MetaTrader 5 broker can operate as a liquidity provider for you. For connection, you only need to open a regular trading account with that broker. Detailed instructions on how to configure gateways are available in the platform [documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/components/gateways).

Modules of allthese gateways are included in the standard platform package. You can test them in a demo mode by creating a configuration in MetaTrader 5 Administrator.

To purchase a gateway, please go to the App [Store](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/market) section in the MetaQuotes Support Center. Also, the App Store features additional solutions for connecting liquidity from third-party developers.

Having selected a data provider, create a new configuration in the Gateway section:

Specify the basic gateway parameters under the **Common** section:

- · **Enable** — enable/disable the gateway. For the gateways running in service mode via the "Remote gateway" module, unchecking Enable will lead to disconnection of platform servers from the gateway service, while the service itself will not be stopped.
- · **Name** — the name of the gateway. Special characters (?, \*, <, >, etc.) are not allowed in the name as these characters can lead to problems in working with the gateway log files.
- · **ID** — specify the unique gateway identifier in this field. The identifier will be specified in the Dealer field of the deals executed via this gateway. This identifier is also used when creating trade request routing rules. The identifier can't be changed in an already created gateway configuration. To change the identifier, create a new configuration and delete the old one.
- · **Module** — the name of the gateway executable. Select here one of the available gateway executable files available in the */gateways* folder of the history server. An unlimited number of configurations with different settings can be created for each module. In the field to the right, select one of the operating modes supported by the gateway:
  - ·**Trade and Quotes**. In this mode, the gateway transmits quotes and processes trading operations.
  - · **Trade only**. In this mode the gateway only processes trading operations. This mode can be used when you work with the externaltrading system using several accounts in this system. This requires creating

several configurations of the same gateway. Only one configuration provides quotes, while all other configurations process trading operations.

- ·**Trade server** — address of the server of the externaltrading system to which the gateway connects.
- ·**Trading login** — account login for connecting to the externaltreading system.
- ·**Password** — the account password for connecting to the externaltreading system.

The gateway ID must not match any of existing manager [accounts.](#page-75-0) When you add a new gateway or edit an existing one, the system checks the validity of the gateway ID. If the ID value is invalid, the gateway configuration will not be added or will not be updated.

Using the **Allow importing traders balances** option, the gateway can be allowed/denied to change and adjust trader balances in the specifies groups. This option is used when the external system to which the gateway connects calculates the financialresults for trading accounts (for example, it can calculate and adjust balances at the end of the trading day).

Turn on the **Allow importing symbol settings** option to enable the gateway to import into the platform the symbols for which it provides data and executes trading operations. The import is performed as follows:

- ·If the symbol does not exist in the trading platform, it is created in the Preliminary group.
- · All newly added symbols are imported with the trading option disabled. The platform administrator must check allthe settings and manually enable trading.
- ·If the symbol already exists in the platform, its trading settings will be updated.

Automatic import of symbol settings greatly simplifies the work of the platform administrator. Instead of the manual addition of all settings, you can simply move symbols from the Preliminary group the desired group and allow trading.

When the gateway changes symbol settings, the following record is printed in the server journal: "symbol config updated". The name of the gateway is indicated as the IP address of the source in such records (the **IP** field).

- · When the **Allow importing symbol settings** option is enabled, the gateway can add and edit any symbols in the Preliminary\\* group, even if the group is not indicated in the list above.
- ·Balance and symbol import functions must be supported by the gateway.

All data feeds and gateways have a standard set of supported parameters.

- · **NewsCategory** — news categories. Here, you can specify the name for the news category delivered from the data source. The category name can then be used for specifying news to be delivered to specific client groups.
- · **Quotes Delay** — a delay in quote transmission, in seconds. The maximum value of quotes delay is 20 minutes (1200 seconds). The density of the quote stream is not reduced and the steam itself is not changed. A quote is passed to the MetaTrader 5 history server only after the expiration of the delay from the moment the quote arrived to Gateway API. If the delay parameter is not defined, the quote delay is not used. Changes in Market Depth and price statistics are delayed together with the quotes stream.
- · **Quotes Tickstats Sample** — the minimum period for sending price statistics, in milliseconds. This parameter allows reducing the frequency of price statistics updates to optimize the traffic.
- · **Quotes Ticks Sample** — the minimum period for sending quotes, in milliseconds. This parameter allows reducing the frequency of quote updates to reduce the traffic. This parameter is recommended to be used only on demo servers.
- · **Quotes Books Sample** — the minimum period for sending Market Depth changes, in milliseconds This parameter allows reducing the frequency of Market Depth updates to reduce the traffic. This parameter is recommended to be used only on demo servers.
- · **Trading Calendar Holidays** — exchanges and trading venues may have working and non-working days that are different from working calendar settings in MetaTrader 5. This parameter overrides working/nonworking days for the gateway.

To add a non-working day, specify a value of the form +DDMMM. The date is specified as two digits, the month is specified as the first three letters of the month name in English. For example, +01JAN. To add a working day, specify a value of the format of -DDMMM, for example, -07FEB. You can specify multiple working/non-working days separated by semicolons, such as + 01JAN;-07FEB. If the added working day does not fall within the [platform](#page-214-0) working hours or trading/quote sessions of instruments, you should update the corresponding settings.

Parameters for reducing the price stream density can be used in conjunction with the **Quotes Delay** parameter. The range of allowable values is 100 – 3,000 milliseconds.

If an incorrect value is specified for a parameter, this parameter will not be used.

#### **Additional network settings for gateways and data feeds**

Additional network settings include history/trade server to gateway/data feed connection parameters. These settings enable the safe operation between the components. In most cases, the parameters are hidden and do not require configuration (the history server sets the required address and connection parameters).

These parameters must be specified in two cases: when working in the remote datafeed/gateway mode, and if the automatically selected address/port is busy. In the second case, an additional message is displayed in the log:

datafeed address 'Data Feed name' already used, please setup another address for datafeed. gateway address 'Gateway name' already used, please setup another address for gateway.

To set connection parameters, select **Show additional network settings** in the **Common** section of the gateway or data feed.

- · **Gateway server** — the address at which the gateway accepts connections from the history and trade servers. The system will automatically insert in this field available addresses of the history server network interfaces. The special address history.server:port is also available in the list. For example, history.server:12345. Specific features of this address:
  - · The gateway/data feed will accept connections on the specified port on the same addresses on which the history server is running (which are specified in the listening address section on the **Network** tab of the history server).
  - · Trade servers will connect to the gateway/data feed though public points (which are specified in the listening address section on the **Network** tab of the history server).
  - · If 0.0.0.0 is present among the listen addresses of the history server, then the gateway willrun exactly on this address. 0.0.0.0 means listening on all addresses.
  - · This method for specifying the address enables the automatic switching of the history server with configured local gateways/data feeds to the backup server without the need to configure their addresses manually.

- · **Gateway login** — the login to authorize the history and trade servers on the gateway/data feed. Only positive numbers can be used as a login.
- · **Password** — the password to authorize the history and trade servers on the gateway/data feed. The password must meet complexity requirements (be at least 6 characters long and use at least two of three available character types: lowercase letters, uppercase letters, and digits).

The address 127.0.0.1 or localhost can also be specified as the gateway server. This address is the so-called [Loopback](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loopback) or a virtual network interface not associated with any hardware. Such addresses are used by default when the gateway, history server and trade servers are running on the same computer. If these addresses are used, the platform performs the following additional checks to ensure proper operation:

- 1. Retrieves lists of addresses listened to by the history and trade servers
- 2. If at least one trade server has no common address with the history server, it is considered that at least one platform component is installed on another physical computer.
- 3. In this case, the gateway is not started on localhost (127.0.0.1), but on the set of listen addresses of the history server. The port specified under "Gateway server" is used for the port. For example, of address 127.0.0.1:16387 is specified for the port and the history server is running on 192.168.0.1:442, the gateway will eventually run on 192.168.0.1:16387.
- 4. When connecting to a gateway/data feed, the trade server also determines to which address to connect (similar to points 1 and 2): Loopack or a set of addresses. The port specified under "Gateway server" is used for the port. The following addresses are used for the set (in order of priority):
  - ·History server public addresses
  - · Local addresses listened to by the history server; these addresses match its public points (are on the same subnet).

If you install a gateway/data feed as a service on a Loopback address, then after transferring any platform component to another computer, the gateway/data feed will become unavailable for that component.

## <span id="page-248-0"></span>**Changing symbols names and markups**

The gateway receives prices from an external system and transmits them to clients adjusted for markups. Through markups, the brokerage company receives its profit share from each deal performed in the external system. Markup values are set separately for Bid and Ask prices by each symbol:

| Parameters   |        |
| Timeouts     |        |
|              |        |

|              |        |

Other text in the form can appear between the tables. The content below relates to configuration of data transmission and symbols.

| Up                      | Down    |
|-------------------------|---------|
| Symbol<br><b>EURUSD</b> | Gateway |
|                         |         |
|                         |         |

The next set shows additional symbol configuration details.

| Add |
|-----|
|     |
|     |

Details of specific symbols include

|  | Symbol        | Source    | Bid | Ask |
|--|---------------|-----------|-----|-----|
|  | <b>EURUSD</b> | EURUSDEXT | -3  | 2   |
|  | <b>GBPUSD</b> | GBPUSDEXT | -2  | 3   |

Options include Add, Edit, Delete, and buttons like OK, Cancel, and Help.

You can also configure matching between symbol names used in the external system with the names used in your MetaTrader 5 platform. For example, if the original symbol name is EURUSDEXT but in the MetaTrader 5 platform it should be called EURUSD, enter EURUSD in the "Symbol" field and EURUSDEXT in the Source box.

The above screenshot shows price translation: at every tick, the Bid price will be reduced by 3 points and the Ask price will be increased by 2 points. Below is a schematic example of the translation:

| External system     | >>> | ask price | EURUSD<br>0.83004 | >>> | MetaTrader 5 server |
|---------------------|-----|-----------|-------------------|-----|---------------------|
| MetaTrader 5 server | >>> | ask price | EURUSD<br>0.83006 | >>> | Client terminal     |
| Client terminal     | >>> | buy limit | EURUSD<br>0.83006 | >>> | MetaTrader 5 server |

| MetaTrader 5 server | >>> | buy limit           | EURUSD<br>0.83004 | >>> | External system     |
|---------------------|-----|---------------------|-------------------|-----|---------------------|
| External system     | >>> | buy limit execution | EURUSD<br>0.83004 | >>> | MetaTrader 5 server |
| MetaTrader 5 server | >>> | buy limit execution | EURUSD<br>0.83006 | >>> | Client terminal     |

The broker earns a profit of 2 pips in this example. The price is sent to the client terminal only after the correction, so the clients work only with the corrected prices. If no correction is set for a symbol, the client will work with the original prices provided by an external system.

Conversion in data feeds is implemented in a similar way. The only difference is that the conversion only affects the transmitted quotes, since data feeds do not work with trading operations.

Translation settings also extend to the Depth of Market. Consider an example where Bid is –10 and Ask is 10. The Depth of Market contains sell orders at prices 120 and 110, as well as by orders at prices 90 and 80. As a result of the translation, the prices of the sell orders will become 130 and 120, and the prices of the buy orders will become 80 and 70.

See also: [Documentation](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/administration/admin_gateways/gateway_translation) / Platform / Platform settings / Gateways / Symbol and price translation

The system parameters are set in the **Timeouts** section.

- ·**Interval between reconnections** — time between attempts to connect to an external server.
- · **Number of reconnection attempts** — how many times the system willtry to connect to an external server. If connection could not succeed after a series of attempts, the system will stop trying for the time specified in the below field.
- · **Interval between series of reconnections** — if connection could not be established after the specified number of attempts, the system will stop trying for the specified time. After this time has elapsed, the system will make another series of reconnection attempts.

## <span id="page-251-0"></span>**Deep price history**

Deep price history is essentialfor traders. It enables in-depth testing and technical analysis. If not sure in the correctness of trading decisions, a trader can refuse to open a real account. Another important factor is the quality of the price history. For example, incorrect spreads or their total unavailability can significantly reduce the trading robots testing quality, since the strategy tester in client terminals does not simulate spreads but takes them directly from history.

MetaTrader 5 features allthe necessary tools to provide complete and high-quality data to traders:

- · There is a universal solution for alltraders enabling access to price history. Everything needed for work is always available in the terminal, not requiring any additional actions from traders. As soon as the historical data is needed for the chart or for the strategy tester, the missing data is downloaded in the maximum traffic efficiency mode.
- ·The history server monitors the data integrity and filters information if necessary.
- · Due to the centralized price data storage, users can run distributed testing and optimization on remote agents and in MQL5 Cloud [Network](https://cloud.mql5.com/). Agents receive computationaltasks, download history from cloud servers and run testing.

The broker only needs to upload a deep price history to the server once. This can be done using data feeds with history import support (for example, IQFeeder), a function for synchronizing data with other MetaTrader servers and a data import function.

#### **How one-minute data is stored**

Only one-minute bars are stored in the platform; all other timeframes are built in client terminals (including mobile and web platforms) using these bars. The use of one-minute bars saves disk space and network traffic, as well as maintains data consistency across alltimeframes. After downloading the price history, the terminal only downloads new data.

Other timeframe charts are quickly plotted based on one-minute bars. Such plotted timeframes are cached on the user's disk. Cached timeframes are even faster to open, since the calculation is performed only for new data. When one-minute bars are changed on the server, the timeframes previously calculated and cached on client terminals will be automatically updated.

The price history is transmitted to client terminals in a compressed form, which significantly saves traffic and minimizes the download time. For example, a 10-year price history of one-minute bars for one symbol is about 10 MB in a compressed form.

The price data received from gateways and data feeds is stored in [history server installation directory\history]. If the free disk space on the history server drops below 2 gigabytes, the system will not save newly received prices. This prevents data from taking up all available space. Thus, the overall server performance is preserved. If data can't be written to disk, the following message is added into the history server log: "'EURUSD' save skipped due not enough free space on disk", "bars and ticks are not saved due not enough free space on disk", "synchronization was stopped due not enough free space on disk." In this case, you should immediately increase free disk space on the server.

#### **How one-minute data is formed**

The history server builds bars based on ticks received from data feeds and gateways. Depending on the [Charts](#page-204-0) parameter of a trading symbol, bars are built using Bid or Last prices (the price of the last executed trade). As a rule, charts of exchange instruments with the enabled Market Depth feature are based on the Last price.

Bars are formed and accumulated only using new incoming ticks. Bar history can only be imported.

## **Tick history**

In addition to one-minute data, the trading platform can also accumulate the history of allreceived quotes, i.e. ticks. Ticks enable traders to test their trading strategies in even more detail, practically in real conditions.

The trading platform can store two types of ticks: raw and accepted. Raw include ticks received directly from data feeds/gateways. Accepted are the ticks that were filtered and converted in accordance with [symbol](#page-234-0) [settings.](#page-234-0)

Accepted ticks are always saved on the history server. The saving of raw ticks depends on the "Save raw prices" parameter in symbol settings:

## **History synchronization with other MetaTrader 4/5 servers**

One of the easiest ways to obtain a deep price history is to set up data synchronization with another MetaTrader server.

MetaQuotes has a permanently running demo server where any user can open a demo account and try MetaTrader 5. The server features financial symbol data that has been carefully collected for a long time. It provides one of the deepest and most correct historical data for many popular forex pairs.

For example, the server stores EURUSD full one-minute history starting from around 1990. Furthermore, it additionally stores daily data (one-day bars) down to 1971.

This server stores deep history for 35 forex pairs, 35 CFDs, XAUUSD and XAGUSD metals. Historical data include Bid prices, spreads (which actually means the availability of Ask prices), and tick volumes.

You can easily download this data to your server for free by synchronizing data with the MetaQuotes-Demo sever. The platform provides a ready configuration for this synchronization under the **Synchronization** section. To receive the data to your server, simply run the **Synchronize history** command in the **Services** menu. This command will download the relevant data to your server. If necessary, you can change some settings in the configuration before the operation, for example, you can set the desired time range.

We will consider later how the synchronization works and how it should be configured.

Open the **Synchronization** section in MetaTrader 5 Administrator and add a new configuration:

In the **Common** section, specify data for connection to the external server and synchronization parameters:

- ·**Enable** — enable or disable data synchronization with this server.
- ·**Server** — server address and port, separated by a colon.
- · **Type** — the type of the server with which synchronization will be performed: MetaTrader 4 or MetaTrader 5.
- · **Login** — the account number on the server with which you synchronize. Use a regular client account which has access to required symbols.

- ·**Password** — password to the account on the server with which you synchronize.
- · **Mode** — data saving mode on your server. In the **Replace** mode, data from your server will be fully replaced with the data from the external server in the specified time range. In the **Combine** mode, only the data missing on your server will be downloaded from the external server, while the existing history will bot be replaced.
- ·**Synchronize** — data type for synchronization: minute data, ticks or both.
- · **Time zone correction** — this function is used when synchronizing data between MetaTrader servers located in different time zones. The **Auto Detect** option is suitable in most cases. The difference in time zones between the servers will be determined automatically to enable correct data saving.
- · **Limits** — you should carefully specify the time interval in which the data will be synchronized so as not to erase your own history. It is recommended to specify 1971.01.01 as the starting date (From), and the date from which a detailed one-minute history is available on your server as the end date.
- · **Check quotation sessions** — if this option is enabled, the system during synchronization willtake into account quoting sessions specified in your platform. If the source server contains price data that does not fall into the quoting sessions of your symbols, such data will not be synchronized (will be ignored). Thus, only price data within the specified quoting sessions will be downloaded to the trading platform.

See also: Documentation / Platform / Platform settings / [Synchronization](https://support.metaquotes.net/en/docs/mt5/platform/administration/admin_synchronization/synchronization_features) / Synchronization features

#### **Importing minute data**

Historical data import has the following objectives:

- ·Generating history when a new symbol is added
- ·Filling in the missing parts of an existing symbol's history
- ·Correcting individualfragments of history, if necessary

Historical data can be imported from a single file or from multiple files simultaneously (from a folder).

Only one-minute bars are stored in the platform; all other timeframes are built in client terminals based on these bars. You can import data from higher timeframes (for example when switching from MetaTrader 4). However, please note that lower timeframe charts will be incomplete. For example, if you import D1 data, these quotes will be written as 1-minute bars as of the beginning of corresponding days. D1 and higher timeframes will provide complete data, while lower timeframe charts will have gaps.
